- entire:teach: Use when a developer wants a topic-focused guided lesson built from canonical checkpoints, not a whole-repo overview. Triggers on phrases like "teach me <topic>", "teach me how this repo handles", "how does <topic> work in this repo", "give me a lesson on", "school me on", and "I need to learn about"
- entire:using-entire: Use for any codebase exploration or understanding task — reads historical intent from Entire checkpoints instead of guessing. Orchestrates other Entire skills to give the agent provenance-backed answers about code.
- entire:what-happened: Explain why code looks the way it does by tracing the latest change for a file range or pasted snippet through `git blame` and deduplicated `entire explain` lookups. Use when the user asks what happened, says "tell me why" about a code block, is confused about a section of code, asks "wtf is going on", "why is this like this", "why was this changed", or wants provenance for a specific file block.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.content:
1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 — the byte-vs-rune lot — were fixed together; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). The remainder is unfixed and reachable from the current code.
16	
17	### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not
18	
19	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`
20	
21	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
22	comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
23	enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.
24	
25	A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
26	grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by
27	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable`.
28	
29	**Fix:** carry a `locked` flag on the modal and make the toggle a no-op when set,
30	or drop the claim from the doc comment.
31	
32	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
33	
34	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
35	
36	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
37	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
38	
39	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
40	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
41	than a drive-by fix.
42	
43	### D5 — Unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`
44	
45	`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:221-223`
46	
47	After cycling the resource type, the code clamps `focusedField` down to
48	`maxField()`. The surrounding branch only runs when `focusedField == 0`, and
49	`maxField()` is never below 4, so the clamp can never fire.
50	
51	Dead defensive code. Harmless, but it implies a state transition that cannot
52	happen and is misleading to read.
53	
54	### D7 — `extractTarGz` keeps parent references in archive paths
55	
56	`internal/oci/oci.go:262`
57	
58	Extraction strips leading `./` and `/` but does not reject `..`, so an archive
59	member named `../../etc/passwd` survives as a map key containing parent
60	references.
61	
62	**Not exploitable today.** The sole consumer, `applyTemplate` in
63	`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go:1053`, turns the map into GitLab commit
64	actions rather than writing to disk, and the server validates the paths.
65	
66	Recorded because the hazard is latent: any future caller that writes these keys
67	under a target directory inherits a Zip Slip. Pinned by
68	`TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys`.
69	
70	**Fix:** reject entries whose cleaned path escapes the root, before returning
71	them.
72	
73	### 1.1 Fixed
74	
75	**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
76	looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
77	fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.
78	
79	Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
80	`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
81	the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
82	terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
83	ones.
84	
85	A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
86	in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
87	Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
88	gone.
89	
90	The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
91	(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
92	`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).
93	
94	One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
95	`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
96	so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
97	theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.
98	
99	**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
100	planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.
101	
102	The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
103	credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
104	unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
105	credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
106	same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
107	won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
108	after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
109	strips the path before the helper is ever called.
110	
111	**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
112	the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
113	change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
114	`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.
115	
116	Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
117	path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
118	contexts anyway.
119	
120	Two smaller defects went with it:
121	
122	- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
123	  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
124	  hang indefinitely.
125	- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
126	  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
127	  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
128	  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.
129	
130	`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
131	than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
132	`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
133	common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command
134	`credential-store --file=/path` — and it hardcoded `protocol=https`, unlike
135	`GitCredentialStorage`, which reads the scheme from the URL.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## 2. Technical debt
140	
141	### Test coverage
142	
143	Currently **18.2 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %, which needs roughly
144	**+7 250 covered statements** over today's ~2 100.
145	
146	Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:
147	
148	| Phase | Scope | Status |
149	|---|---|---|
150	| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
151	| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **done** except the `ui/theme` complement (~55 stmts) |
152	| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | pending (~1 240 stmts) |
153	| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | pending (~2 470 stmts) |
154	| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | pending (~1 995 stmts) |
155	| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | pending (~1 360 stmts) |
156	| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending (~400 stmts) |
157	
158	Phase 1 progress:
159	
160	| Package | Before | Now |
161	|---|---|---|
162	| `internal/ui/testutil` | — | **100 %** (new) |
163	| `internal/ui/shortcut` | 0 % | **100 %** |
164	| `internal/ui/help` | 0 % | **96.7 %** |
165	| `internal/ui/components` | 0 % | **79.8 %** |
166	| `internal/oci` | 0 % | **33.6 %** |
167	| `internal/docker` | 7.3 % | **65.4 %** (phase 5, pulled forward — see below) |
168	| `internal/gitlab` | 7.5 % | **100 %** |
169	| `internal/credentials` | 29.5 % | **98.2 %** |
170	
171	`internal/oci` stops at 33.6 % because the remaining statements are registry HTTP
172	paths (`DownloadTemplate`, `listCatalog`, `ListTemplates`) that need a fuller
173	`httptest` fixture — a manifest plus a gzipped layer — rather than the
174	single-response stubs used so far.
175	
176	Phase 5's blocker is cleared for `docker`: the package now routes every CLI
177	invocation through the `dockerRunner` seam in `internal/docker/exec.go`, so tests
178	drive argument building and output parsing against canned output. `scan` and
179	`app` remain.
180	
181	`internal/gitlab` needed no seam: every function takes a `*gitlabclient.Client`
182	built from a base URL, so an `httptest` server standing in for the API covers
183	the whole package. `Clone` is exercised against a throwaway local repository
184	rather than mocked, and skips when no `git` binary is on `PATH`.
185	
186	`internal/credentials` needed no seam either. `git credential` is steerable
187	through the environment, so the tests redirect `HOME`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and
188	`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` at a temporary directory and run the real binary against a
189	throwaway `store` helper — nothing reaches the developer's keychain. Running the
190	real git is what surfaced the context-isolation defect recorded in §1.1; a stub
191	would have frozen the broken behaviour instead. The 2 s timeout is covered by
192	installing a credential helper that sleeps.
193	
194	### Files over the 800-line ceiling
195	
196	The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Seven exceed it:
197	
198	| File | Lines |
199	|---|---|
200	| `internal/ui/security/model.go` | 1785 |
201	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` | 1556 |
202	| `internal/app/app.go` | 1333 |
203	| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` | 1214 |
204	| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | 1133 |
205	| `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` | 995 |
206	| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go` | 822 |
207	
208	`internal/docker/client.go` (1176 lines — the 1069 recorded earlier was stale)
209	was split into `exec.go`, `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`,
210	`volumes.go`, `registry.go`, `launch.go`, `system.go` and `parse.go`; the largest
211	is now 269 lines. The former `network.go` became `ports.go`, since it reports the
212	host's listening sockets via `ss` rather than Docker networks — the name was
213	free for the `docker network` family.
214	
215	This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
216	tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
217	Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
218	7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.
219	
220	### Race detector cannot run locally
221	
222	`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
223	it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
224	concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.
225	
226	**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
227	every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
228	run reported no data race across all 17 packages.
229	
230	That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
231	tests actually execute, and coverage is 18.2 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
232	paths — most of the view layer — remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so
233	this is an argument for the coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.
234	
235	Installing a local toolchain is still worth doing for anyone touching `Cmd`s, to
236	avoid learning about a race from CI after the fact.
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 3. Planned features
241	
242	Carried over from `todo.md`.
243	
244	### 3.1 Network diagnostics
245	
246	- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
247	  redirections to the host machine.
248	
249	### 3.2 Interactive security remediation
250	
251	- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
252	  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
253	- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
254	  directly into the Workspace view.
255	
256	### 3.3 OCI build and cache analyser
257	
258	- **Layer visualisation** — analyse a local image and show the size of each
259	  layer, in the spirit of `dive`. Intended approach:
260	  - Integrated via `google/go-containerregistry` ("daemonless", no dependency on
261	    the Docker daemon).
262	  - Talk to OCI registries directly, pulling manifests and configs without
263	    downloading the whole image.
264	  - Stream layers in memory (`tar`) to rebuild the filesystem tree.
265	  - Compute wasted space by detecting whiteout files (`.wh.`).
266	- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.
267	  "`package.json` changed, invalidating the cache".
268	
269	### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers
270	
271	- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
272	  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
273	- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
274	  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.
275	
276	### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)
277	
278	- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
279	  for every container in the selected project.
280	- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).
281	
282	### 3.6 GitHub support alongside GitLab, one active forge per context
283	
284	Support GitHub as well as GitLab, with **exactly one backend active per
285	configuration context**. A context targets one forge; switching forge means
286	switching context.
287	
288	Not started. The notes below are what the current code imposes on the design,
289	not a chosen design.
290	
291	#### What is coupled to GitLab today
292	
293	| Surface | Size |
294	|---|---|
295	| `internal/gitlab` + `internal/ui/gitlab/{auth,explorer}` | ~3 900 lines |
296	| Direct uses of `*gitlabclient.Client` outside `internal/gitlab` | 66, across 8 files |
297	
298	The concrete SDK type leaks into `internal/shared/state.go:57`
299	(`GitLabClient *gitlabclient.Client`), so every consumer is bound to go-gitlab
300	rather than to a DevDesk abstraction. That field is the load-bearing change: an
301	interface there is what makes a second forge possible at all.
302	
303	Also GitLab-shaped: `GitLabConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:41` (URL, token,
304	clone method, pull settings), the `gitlab-auth` / `gitlab-explorer` view names
305	and their `gla` / `gle` aliases in `internal/command/parser.go`, and
306	`shared.GitLabStats`.
307	
308	#### Model mismatches to settle before coding
309	
310	These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
311	promise.
312	
313	- **Nesting.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups → projects. GitHub
314	  has no nested groups: an organisation holds repositories, flat. Either the
315	  tree degrades to two levels for GitHub, or the abstraction exposes a depth the
316	  backend declares.
317	- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
318	  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
319	  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
320	  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there — see also D2.
321	- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
322	  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
323	  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
324	  limits and semantics.
325	- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
326	  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
327	  applies either way.
328	
329	#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs
330	
331	Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
332	package needs a seam.
333	
334	Arguments for the CLIs:
335	
336	- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
337	  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
338	  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
339	- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
340	  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
341	- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.

# DevDesk Backlog

**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02

Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
rather than carried over.

---

## 1. Known defects

D1, D3 and D6 — the byte-vs-rune lot — were fixed together; see
[§1.1](#11-fixed). The remainder is unfixed and reachable from the current code.

### D2 — The "permanent delete" checkbox is documented as locked but is not

`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:35` and `:99-105`

`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent` pre-checks *Immediate deletion* and its doc
comment states the box is non-modifiable ("pré-cochée et non modifiable"). Nothing
enforces that: `space` and `enter` on the checkbox still toggle it.

A project already marked for deletion can therefore be sent through a
grace-period delete that the caller does not expect. Pinned by
`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable`.

**Fix:** carry a `locked` flag on the modal and make the toggle a no-op when set,
or drop the claim from the doc comment.

### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation

`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`

`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.

Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
than a drive-by fix.

### D5 — Unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`

`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:221-223`

After cycling the resource type, the code clamps `focusedField` down to
`maxField()`. The surrounding branch only runs when `focusedField == 0`, and
`maxField()` is never below 4, so the clamp can never fire.

Dead defensive code. Harmless, but it implies a state transition that cannot
happen and is misleading to read.

### D7 — `extractTarGz` keeps parent references in archive paths

`internal/oci/oci.go:262`

Extraction strips leading `./` and `/` but does not reject `..`, so an archive
member named `../../etc/passwd` survives as a map key containing parent
references.

**Not exploitable today.** The sole consumer, `applyTemplate` in
`internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go:1053`, turns the map into GitLab commit
actions rather than writing to disk, and the server validates the paths.

Recorded because the hazard is latent: any future caller that writes these keys
under a target directory inherits a Zip Slip. Pinned by
`TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys`.

**Fix:** reject entries whose cleaned path escapes the root, before returning
them.

### 1.1 Fixed

**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.

Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
ones.

A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
gone.

The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).

One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.

**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.

The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
strips the path before the helper is ever called.

**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would
change credential resolution for every repository on the machine. Pinned by
`TestGitCredentialIsolatesContexts`.

Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
contexts anyway.

Two smaller defects went with it:

- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
  hang indefinitely.
- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.

`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command
`credential-store --file=/path` — and it hardcoded `protocol=https`, unlike
`GitCredentialStorage`, which reads the scheme from the URL.

---

## 2. Technical debt

### Test coverage

Currently **18.2 %** overall; the agreed target is 80 %, which needs roughly
**+7 250 covered statements** over today's ~2 100.

Phased plan, with the harness and most of phase 1 delivered:

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **done** except the `ui/theme` complement (~55 stmts) |
| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | pending (~1 240 stmts) |
| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | pending (~2 470 stmts) |
| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | pending (~1 995 stmts) |
| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | pending (~1 360 stmts) |
| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | pending (~400 stmts) |

Phase 1 progress:

| Package | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/testutil` | — | **100 %** (new) |
| `internal/ui/shortcut` | 0 % | **100 %** |
| `internal/ui/help` | 0 % | **96.7 %** |
| `internal/ui/components` | 0 % | **79.8 %** |
| `internal/oci` | 0 % | **33.6 %** |
| `internal/docker` | 7.3 % | **65.4 %** (phase 5, pulled forward — see below) |
| `internal/gitlab` | 7.5 % | **100 %** |
| `internal/credentials` | 29.5 % | **98.2 %** |

`internal/oci` stops at 33.6 % because the remaining statements are registry HTTP
paths (`DownloadTemplate`, `listCatalog`, `ListTemplates`) that need a fuller
`httptest` fixture — a manifest plus a gzipped layer — rather than the
single-response stubs used so far.

Phase 5's blocker is cleared for `docker`: the package now routes every CLI
invocation through the `dockerRunner` seam in `internal/docker/exec.go`, so tests
drive argument building and output parsing against canned output. `scan` and
`app` remain.

`internal/gitlab` needed no seam: every function takes a `*gitlabclient.Client`
built from a base URL, so an `httptest` server standing in for the API covers
the whole package. `Clone` is exercised against a throwaway local repository
rather than mocked, and skips when no `git` binary is on `PATH`.

`internal/credentials` needed no seam either. `git credential` is steerable
through the environment, so the tests redirect `HOME`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and
`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` at a temporary directory and run the real binary against a
throwaway `store` helper — nothing reaches the developer's keychain. Running the
real git is what surfaced the context-isolation defect recorded in §1.1; a stub
would have frozen the broken behaviour instead. The 2 s timeout is covered by
installing a credential helper that sleeps.

### Files over the 800-line ceiling

The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Seven exceed it:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `internal/ui/security/model.go` | 1785 |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/update.go` | 1556 |
| `internal/app/app.go` | 1333 |
| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/model.go` | 1214 |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | 1133 |
| `internal/ui/netdiag/model.go` | 995 |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go` | 822 |

`internal/docker/client.go` (1176 lines — the 1069 recorded earlier was stale)
was split into `exec.go`, `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`,
`volumes.go`, `registry.go`, `launch.go`, `system.go` and `parse.go`; the largest
is now 269 lines. The former `network.go` became `ports.go`, since it reports the
host's listening sockets via `ss` rather than Docker networks — the name was
free for the `docker network` family.

This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.

### Race detector cannot run locally

`mise run test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler on `PATH`. Without one
it fails with `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found`. Bubble Tea `Cmd`s run
concurrently, so this is the check most likely to catch a Rule 110 violation.

**Now covered by CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mise run test-race` on
every push and pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`, which has a toolchain. The first
run reported no data race across all 17 packages.

That is a baseline, not a clean bill of health: the detector only sees code the
tests actually execute, and coverage is 18.2 %. Rule 110 violations in untested
paths — most of the view layer — remain invisible. The two efforts compound, so
this is an argument for the coverage phases rather than a substitute for them.

Installing a local toolchain is still worth doing for anyone touching `Cmd`s, to
avoid learning about a race from CI after the fact.

---

## 3. Planned features

Carried over from `todo.md`.

### 3.1 Network diagnostics

- **Port-forwarding manager** — an interactive dashboard to manage port
  redirections to the host machine.

### 3.2 Interactive security remediation

- **Auto-patch assistance** — after a Trivy scan, offer to generate a patch or an
  updated `Dockerfile` that bumps the base image version to clear critical CVEs.
- **Local SAST** — wire security linters (Gitleaks for secrets, IaC linters)
  directly into the Workspace view.

### 3.3 OCI build and cache analyser

- **Layer visualisation** — analyse a local image and show the size of each
  layer, in the spirit of `dive`. Intended approach:
  - Integrated via `google/go-containerregistry` ("daemonless", no dependency on
    the Docker daemon).
  - Talk to OCI registries directly, pulling manifests and configs without
    downloading the whole image.
  - Stream layers in memory (`tar`) to rebuild the filesystem tree.
  - Compute wasted space by detecting whiteout files (`.wh.`).
- **Cache-miss analysis** — explain why a build's cache was invalidated, e.g.
  "`package.json` changed, invalidating the cache".

### 3.4 Spontaneous dev containers

- **Configuration injection** — inject the developer's dotfiles (vim, zsh,
  aliases) when opening a terminal inside a container.
- **Hot volume mount** — mount the current working directory into a running
  container on the fly, to test a local script without rebuilding the image.

### 3.5 Resource dashboard (embedded mini-htop)

- **TUI charts** — braille-character charts showing live CPU, RAM and network I/O
  for every container in the selected project.
- **Visual alerts** — user-defined thresholds (e.g. memory saturation).

### 3.6 GitHub support alongside GitLab, one active forge per context

Support GitHub as well as GitLab, with **exactly one backend active per
configuration context**. A context targets one forge; switching forge means
switching context.

Not started. The notes below are what the current code imposes on the design,
not a chosen design.

#### What is coupled to GitLab today

| Surface | Size |
|---|---|
| `internal/gitlab` + `internal/ui/gitlab/{auth,explorer}` | ~3 900 lines |
| Direct uses of `*gitlabclient.Client` outside `internal/gitlab` | 66, across 8 files |

The concrete SDK type leaks into `internal/shared/state.go:57`
(`GitLabClient *gitlabclient.Client`), so every consumer is bound to go-gitlab
rather than to a DevDesk abstraction. That field is the load-bearing change: an
interface there is what makes a second forge possible at all.

Also GitLab-shaped: `GitLabConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:41` (URL, token,
clone method, pull settings), the `gitlab-auth` / `gitlab-explorer` view names
and their `gla` / `gle` aliases in `internal/command/parser.go`, and
`shared.GitLabStats`.

#### Model mismatches to settle before coding

These are not implementation details; they decide what the abstraction can even
promise.

- **Nesting.** The explorer is a tree of groups → subgroups → projects. GitHub
  has no nested groups: an organisation holds repositories, flat. Either the
  tree degrades to two levels for GitHub, or the abstraction exposes a depth the
  backend declares.
- **Deletion.** `DeleteGroup` / `DeleteProject` implement GitLab's two-step
  permanent delete (schedule, then purge under the renamed
  `-deletion_scheduled-<id>` path). GitHub deletes immediately and has no
  equivalent, so the "permanent" checkbox is meaningless there — see also D2.
- **Dashboard counters.** `FetchDashboardStats` reads `X-Total` from five list
  endpoints. GitHub has no equivalent header for these; the counts come from the
  search API (`search/issues?q=is:open+is:pr+assignee:@me`), with different rate
  limits and semantics.
- **Vocabulary.** Group/project/merge request vs organisation/repository/pull
  request. The UI must pick per-backend labels or a neutral vocabulary; Rule 129
  applies either way.

#### Open decision: Go SDKs or the `gh` / `glab` CLIs

Worth deciding before any code is written, because it determines whether the
package needs a seam.

Arguments for the CLIs:

- Authentication is already solved, including OAuth device flow, self-hosted
  hosts and token storage. DevDesk's own credential handling could shrink — and
  it has already proven fragile (see §1.1).
- `gh api` and `glab api` are raw REST/GraphQL passthroughs, so no SDK is needed
  for coverage of endpoints the abstraction does not model.
- No SDK version churn to track for two forges.

Arguments against:

- **Per-context isolation conflicts with how these tools store auth.** Both keep
  global per-host state (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`). DevDesk contexts want
  *different tokens for the same host*. Driving `gh auth switch` from the TUI
  would mutate the user's global CLI state — the exact mistake avoided in §1.1 by
  scoping `credential.useHttpPath` to the invocation. The clean route is
  `GH_TOKEN` / `GITLAB_TOKEN` per invocation, but then DevDesk still owns the
  tokens and the main benefit is gone.
- **Two more hard dependencies.** Today DevDesk needs `git`, and `docker` only
  for the features that use it. Requiring `gh` and `glab` for the core forge
  feature is a real setup-friction regression.
- **Cost per call.** A process spawn per request, against a reused HTTP
  connection today. The dashboard alone issues five calls, and the explorer
  paginates.
- **Testability regresses.** `internal/gitlab` reaches 100 % with no seam,
  because the SDK takes a base URL that an `httptest` server can stand in for.
  Shelling out would put it back in the position `internal/docker` was in, needing
  a manufactured seam — and stubbed CLI output encodes assumptions about the tool
  rather than testing against it.

**Current recommendation:** keep Go SDKs (go-gitlab, go-github) for the API
surface, and use the CLIs only as an *optional* token source — when a context has
no token, offer to read one from `gh auth token --hostname <host>` or
`glab auth status`. That takes the convenience without the coupling. Recorded as
a recommendation, not a decision.

#### Sketch of the work

1. Define a `forge` abstraction from what the code actually consumes: current
   user, namespace tree, create/delete namespace and repository, initial commit,
   dashboard counters, clone URL.
2. Replace `shared.State.GitLabClient` with that interface. This is the change
   the other 65 call sites follow from.
3. Generalise `GitLabConfig` into a per-context forge config carrying a
   `type: gitlab | github` discriminator, and migrate existing config files.
4. Implement the GitLab backend by moving the existing code behind the
   interface — behaviour-preserving, and covered by the tests added in #7.
5. Implement the GitHub backend.
6. Rename the views and commands, keeping `gla` / `gle` as aliases so muscle
   memory survives.

Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own: they are a refactor of working code with
tests already in place, and they are what makes step 5 tractable.

---

## 4. Existing plans

Detailed plans live in `.claude/plans/`. One is referenced directly from the old
`todo.md` and is still outstanding:

- [`platform_compatibility_improvements.md`](../.claude/plans/platform_compatibility_improvements.md)
  — Docker-layer platform portability.

Backlog lu (`docs/backlog.md`, à jour au 2026-08-02). État réel vérifié dans le code :

**Défauts ouverts** (D1/D3/D6 et l'isolation des credentials sont faits en #5/#8)

| # | Sujet | Poids |
|---|---|---|
| D7 | `extractTarGz` (`internal/oci/oci.go:262`) garde les `..` dans les clés — Zip Slip latent | petit, sécurité |
| D2 | Checkbox « permanent delete » documentée comme verrouillée mais togglable | petit |
| D5 | Clamp de focus mort dans `CreationForm` | trivial |
| D4 | `Tab` pour naviguer entre champs (viole Rule 135) | nécessite un arbitrage UX |

D7 et D2 ont chacun un test « pinned » qui `t.Skip()` dès que le défaut est corrigé (`internal/oci/oci_test.go:161`, `internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal_test.go:202`) — ils sont conçus pour être remplacés par de vraies assertions.

**Dette technique**
- Couverture : 18,2 % global, cible 80 %. Phase 1 close sauf le complément `ui/theme` (à 81 % aujourd'hui, ~55 stmts restants). Phase 2 = `status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth` (~1 240 stmts).
- 7 fichiers > 800 lignes. Le backlog signale lui-même le conflit d'ordre : écrire des milliers de statements de tests contre `security/model.go` (1785) ou `oci_resources/update.go` (1556) fige leur structure avant le split.

**Features** : multi-forge GitHub (étapes 1–4 = refactor de code testé, faisable seul), port-forwarding, dive-like, etc.

Ma recommandation : une PR courte D7 + D2 + D5 d'abord (auto-contenue, deux tests attendent déjà, D7 est le seul à portée sécurité), puis attaquer la phase 2 de couverture. D4 reste en attente d'une décision de ta part.

1	package components
2	
3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
10	)
11	
12	// DeleteConfirmModal est une boîte de dialogue de confirmation pour suppression
13	// avec option de suppression immédiate
14	type DeleteConfirmModal struct {
15		title             string
16		message           string
17		focused           int  // 0 = checkbox, 1 = Yes, 2 = No
18		permanentlyRemove bool // Si true, suppression immédiate sans période de grâce
19		width             int
20		height            int
21	}
22	
23	// NewDeleteConfirmModal crée une nouvelle modal de confirmation de suppression
24	func NewDeleteConfirmModal(title, message string) *DeleteConfirmModal {
25		return &DeleteConfirmModal{
26			title:             title,
27			message:           message,
28			focused:           2, // Default sur "No" pour éviter les suppressions accidentelles
29			permanentlyRemove: false,
30		}
31	}
32	
33	// NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent crée une modal avec la case "immediate deletion" pré-cochée et non modifiable.
34	// À utiliser quand le projet est déjà marqué pour suppression — seule la suppression permanente est possible.
35	func NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent(title, message string) *DeleteConfirmModal {
36		return &DeleteConfirmModal{
37			title:             title,
38			message:           message,
39			focused:           2, // Default sur "No"
40			permanentlyRemove: true,
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg est envoyé quand l'utilisateur confirme la suppression
45	type DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg struct {
46		PermanentlyRemove bool
47	}
48	
49	// DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg est envoyé quand l'utilisateur annule
50	type DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg struct{}
51	
52	// Update met à jour la modal
53	func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*DeleteConfirmModal, tea.Cmd) {
54		switch msg := msg.(type) {
55		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
56			m.width = msg.Width
57			m.height = msg.Height
58	
59		case tea.KeyMsg:
60			switch msg.String() {
61			case "up", "k":
62				// Navigate up
63				if m.focused > 0 {
64					m.focused--
65				}
66				return m, nil
67	
68			case "down", "j":
69				// Navigate down
70				if m.focused < 2 {
71					m.focused++
72				}
73				return m, nil
74	
75			case "left", "h":
76				// Si sur les boutons, aller vers Yes
77				if m.focused == 2 {
78					m.focused = 1
79				}
80				return m, nil
81	
82			case "right", "l":
83				// Si sur les boutons, aller vers No
84				if m.focused == 1 {
85					m.focused = 2
86				}
87				return m, nil
88	
89			case "tab":
90				// Cycle through: checkbox -> Yes -> No -> checkbox
91				m.focused = (m.focused + 1) % 3
92				return m, nil
93	
94			case "shift+tab":
95				// Cycle backwards
96				m.focused = (m.focused + 2) % 3
97				return m, nil
98	
99			case " ":
100				// Toggle checkbox si focus dessus, sinon confirmer la sélection
101				if m.focused == 0 {
102					m.permanentlyRemove = !m.permanentlyRemove
103					return m, nil
104				}
105				return m.handleConfirm()
106	
107			case "enter":
108				return m.handleConfirm()
109	
110			case "y", "Y":
111				// Raccourci pour Yes
112				return m, func() tea.Msg {
113					return DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg{PermanentlyRemove: m.permanentlyRemove}
114				}
115	
116			case "n", "N", "esc":
117				// Raccourci pour No
118				return m, func() tea.Msg {
119					return DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg{}
120				}
121			}
122		}
123	
124		return m, nil
125	}
126	
127	// handleConfirm gère la confirmation selon l'élément sélectionné
128	func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) handleConfirm() (*DeleteConfirmModal, tea.Cmd) {
129		switch m.focused {
130		case 0:
131			// Toggle checkbox
132			m.permanentlyRemove = !m.permanentlyRemove
133			return m, nil
134		case 1:
135			// Yes
136			return m, func() tea.Msg {
137				return DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg{PermanentlyRemove: m.permanentlyRemove}
138			}
139		case 2:
140			// No
141			return m, func() tea.Msg {
142				return DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg{}
143			}
144		}
145		return m, nil
146	}
147	
148	// View affiche la modal
149	func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) View() string {
150		var b strings.Builder
151	
152		// Titre
153		b.WriteString(theme.TitleStyle.Render(m.title))
154		b.WriteString("\n\n")
155	
156		// Message
157		b.WriteString(m.message)
158		b.WriteString("\n\n")
159	
160		// Checkbox pour suppression immédiate
161		checkboxStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground)
162		if m.focused == 0 {
163			checkboxStyle = checkboxStyle.Bold(true).Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight)
164		}
165	
166		checkbox := theme.IconCheckbox
167		if m.permanentlyRemove {
168			checkbox = theme.IconChecked
169		}
170	
171		indicator := "  "
172		if m.focused == 0 {
173			indicator = theme.IconCircleSmall + " "
174		}
175	
176		checkboxLabel := " Immediate deletion (no grace period)"
177		checkboxLine := checkboxStyle.Render(indicator + checkbox + checkboxLabel)
178		b.WriteString(checkboxLine)
179	
180		// Warning si suppression immédiate activée
181		if m.permanentlyRemove {
182			b.WriteString("\n")
183			warningStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight).Italic(true)
184			b.WriteString(warningStyle.Render("  " + theme.IconWarning + " This action is irreversible!"))
185		}
186		b.WriteString("\n\n")
187	
188		// Boutons
189		yes := theme.RenderButton("Yes", m.focused == 1, "danger")
190		no := theme.RenderButton("No", m.focused == 2, "primary")
191	
192		buttons := yes + theme.Bg("  ") + no
193		b.WriteString(buttons)
194		b.WriteString("\n\n")
195	
196		return lipgloss.NewStyle().
197			Background(theme.ColorBackground).
198			Foreground(theme.ColorText).
199			Border(lipgloss.NormalBorder()).
200			BorderForeground(theme.ColorError).
201			BorderBackground(theme.ColorBackground).
202			Padding(1, 2).
203			Render(b.String())
204	}

21	// Init démarre l'application
22	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
23		return tea.Batch(
24			m.spinner.Tick,
25			tickCmd(),
26			checkComponents(m.config),
27		)
28	}
29	
30	// Update gère les messages et met à jour l'état
31	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
32		var cmd tea.Cmd
33		var cmds []tea.Cmd
34	
35		switch msg := msg.(type) {
36		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
37			m.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
38	
39		case tea.KeyMsg:
40			return m.handleInputKeyMsg(msg)
41	
42		case TickMsg:
43			return m.handleTick()
44	
45		case spinner.TickMsg:
46			if m.checking {
47				m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
48				cmds = append(cmds, cmd)
49			}
50	
51		case CheckCompleteMsg:
52			return m.handleCheckComplete(msg)
53	
54		case components.ComponentFormSubmitMsg:
55			return m.handleComponentFormSubmit(msg)
56	
57		case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg:
58			m.componentForm = nil
59			m.creating = false
60			m.editing = false
61	
62		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
63			return m.handleConfirmDelete()
64	
65		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
66			// Annulation de suppression
67			m.confirmModal = nil
68			m.confirming = false
69	
70		case ComponentSavedMsg:
71			return m.handleComponentSaved(msg)
72	
73		case ComponentDeletedMsg:
74			return m.handleComponentDeleted(msg)
75		}
76	
77		// Mettre à jour la table active si pas en mode formulaire/confirmation
78		if m.componentForm == nil && m.confirmModal == nil {
79			if m.activeTab == TabMonitors {
80				m.monitorTable, cmd = m.monitorTable.Update(msg)
81			} else {
82				m.sslTable, cmd = m.sslTable.Update(msg)
83			}
84			cmds = append(cmds, cmd)
85		}
86	
87		return m, tea.Batch(cmds...)
88	}

91	func (m Model) handleTick() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
92		// Rafraîchir la table pour mettre à jour "Last Check"
93		if len(m.components) > 0 {
94			m.updateTable()
95		}
96	
97		// Vérifier si on doit faire un check
98		if !m.paused && !m.checking && time.Now().After(m.nextCheck) {
99			m.checking = true
100			return m, tea.Batch(
101				tickCmd(),
102				checkComponents(m.config),
103			)
104		}
105		return m, tickCmd()
106	}

111		m.firstCheck = false

113		m.nextCheck = msg.Timestamp.Add(m.refreshInterval)
114

117		} else {
118			m.components = msg.Components
119			m.logComponentErrors(msg.Components)
120			m.updateTable()

122			// Recalculer les hauteurs des tables maintenant qu'elles ont des données

127	}

193		m.sslTable.SetHeight(tableDataHeight)

196		contentWidth := m.width - 2
197	
198		// Monitor table columns (5 columns, cell padding = 5×2 = 10)
199		monColumns := m.monitorTable.Columns()
200		if len(monColumns) >= 5 {
201			available := contentWidth - 5*2
202			monColumns[0].Width = int(float64(available) * 0.15) // Name
203			monColumns[1].Width = int(float64(available) * 0.30) // Target
204			monColumns[2].Width = int(float64(available) * 0.17) // Status
205			monColumns[3].Width = int(float64(available) * 0.18) // Type
206			// Dernière colonne récupère le reste pour remplir toute la largeur
207			monColumns[4].Width = available - monColumns[0].Width - monColumns[1].Width - monColumns[2].Width - monColumns[3].Width
208			m.monitorTable.SetColumns(monColumns)

217			sslColumns[2].Width = int(float64(available) * 0.15) // Status
218			sslColumns[3].Width = int(float64(available) * 0.10) // Days Left
219			sslColumns[4].Width = int(float64(available) * 0.18) // Expires
220			// Dernière colonne récupère le reste
221			sslColumns[5].Width = available - sslColumns[0].Width - sslColumns[1].Width - sslColumns[2].Width - sslColumns[3].Width - sslColumns[4].Width
222			m.sslTable.SetColumns(sslColumns)

228		if m.activeTab == TabCertificates {
229			return &m.sslTable

234	// getSelectedComponentIndex returns the actual index in m.config.Status.Components array
235	// accounting for sorting and filtering between monitor and SSL tables
236	func (m *Model) getSelectedComponentIndex() int {
237		cursor := m.getCurrentTable().Cursor()
238	
239		if m.activeTab == TabMonitors {
240			// Get monitors in sorted order, find the one at cursor position
241			var monitors []status.ComponentStatus
242			for _, comp := range m.components {
243				if comp.Type != "ssl" {
244					monitors = append(monitors, comp)
245				}
246			}
247			sorted := m.sortedMonitors(monitors)
248			if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(sorted) {
249				return -1
250			}
251			selected := sorted[cursor]
252			// Find matching config component by name+type+target
253			for i, c := range m.config.Status.Components {
254				if c.Name == selected.Name && string(c.Type) == string(selected.Type) && c.Target == selected.Target {
255					return i
256				}
257			}
258		} else {

269							return j
270						}
271					}
272					return i
273				}

279	}

305		switch msg.String() {

308		case "q", "ctrl+c":
309			return m, tea.Quit
310		case "ctrl+r", " ", "+", "-":

312		case "up", "down", "k", "j", "tab", "shift+tab", "g", "G", "home", "end":

323	// handleRefreshControls handles refresh, pause, and interval adjustments
324	func (m Model) handleRefreshControls(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
325		switch msg.String() {
326		case "ctrl+r":
327			// Refresh immédiat
328			if !m.checking {
329				m.checking = true
330				return m, tea.Batch(
331					m.spinner.Tick,
332					checkComponents(m.config),
333				)
334			}
335	
336		case " ":
337			// Toggle pause
338			m.paused = !m.paused
339			if !m.paused && !m.checking && time.Since(m.lastCheck) >= m.refreshInterval {
340				m.checking = true
341				return m, tea.Batch(
342					m.spinner.Tick,
343					checkComponents(m.config),
344				)
345			}
346	
347		case "+":
348			// Augmenter l'intervalle
349			m.refreshInterval += 5 * time.Second
350			if m.refreshInterval > 300*time.Second {
351				m.refreshInterval = 300 * time.Second
352			}
353	
354		case "-":
355			// Diminuer l'intervalle
356			m.refreshInterval -= 5 * time.Second
357			if m.refreshInterval < 5*time.Second {
358				m.refreshInterval = 5 * time.Second
359			}
360		}
361	
362		return m, nil
363	}

371			m.sslTable.Blur()

385			m.getCurrentTable().MoveUp(1)

402	func (m Model) handleComponentFormSubmit(msg components.ComponentFormSubmitMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
403		m.componentForm = nil
404		if msg.Original != nil {
405			m.editing = false
406			for i, c := range m.config.Status.Components {
407				if c.Name == msg.Original.Name && c.Type == msg.Original.Type && c.Target == msg.Original.Target {
408					m.config.Status.Components[i] = msg.Component
409					break
410				}
411			}
412		} else {
413			m.creating = false
414			m.config.Status.Components = append(m.config.Status.Components, msg.Component)
415		}
416		return m, saveComponent(m.config)
417	}

420	func (m Model) handleConfirmDelete() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
421		m.confirmModal = nil
422		m.confirming = false
423		if m.selectedIdx >= 0 && m.selectedIdx < len(m.config.Status.Components) {
424			m.config.Status.Components = append(
425				m.config.Status.Components[:m.selectedIdx],
426				m.config.Status.Components[m.selectedIdx+1:]...,
427			)
428			return m, deleteComponent(m.config)
429		}

433	// handleMonitorOperations handles new, edit, and delete operations
434	func (m Model) handleMonitorOperations(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
435		switch msg.String() {
436		case "ctrl+n":
437			// Nouveau composant
438			m.creating = true
439			m.componentForm = components.NewComponentForm(nil)
440	
441		case "e":
442			// Éditer le composant sélectionné
443			if len(m.components) > 0 {
444				idx := m.getSelectedComponentIndex()
445				if idx >= 0 && idx < len(m.config.Status.Components) {
446					m.editing = true
447					m.selectedIdx = idx
448					m.componentForm = components.NewComponentForm(&m.config.Status.Components[idx])
449				}
450			}
451	
452		case "ctrl+d":
453			// Supprimer le composant sélectionné
454			if len(m.components) > 0 {
455				idx := m.getSelectedComponentIndex()
456				if idx >= 0 && idx < len(m.config.Status.Components) {
457					m.confirming = true
458					m.selectedIdx = idx
459					compName := m.config.Status.Components[idx].Name
460					m.confirmModal = sharedcomponents.NewConfirmModal(
461						"Delete Monitor",
462						fmt.Sprintf("Are you sure you want to delete '%s'?", compName),
463					)
464				}
465			}
466		}
467	
468		return m, nil
469	}
470	
471	// sortableColumns lists columns in cycle order for the '.' key
472	var sortableColumns = []sortField{
473		sortByName,
474		sortByTarget,
475		sortByType,
476		sortByResponse,
477	}
478	
479	// cycleSort cycles through sort options: each column asc then desc, then next column
480	func (m Model) cycleSort() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
481		if m.sortAsc {
482			m.sortAsc = false
483		} else {
484			m.sortAsc = true
485			nextIdx := 0
486			for i, col := range sortableColumns {
487				if col == m.sortColumn {
488					nextIdx = (i + 1) % len(sortableColumns)
489					break
490				}
491			}
492			m.sortColumn = sortableColumns[nextIdx]
493		}
494		m.updateTable()
495		return m, nil
496	}
497	
498	// sortedMonitors returns monitor components sorted by the current sort column
499	func (m *Model) sortedMonitors(components []status.ComponentStatus) []status.ComponentStatus {
500		sorted := make([]status.ComponentStatus, len(components))
501		copy(sorted, components)
502	
503		sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
504			a, b := sorted[i], sorted[j]
505	
506			var less bool
507			switch m.sortColumn {
508			case sortByTarget:
509				less = strings.ToLower(a.Target) < strings.ToLower(b.Target)
510			case sortByType:
511				less = strings.ToLower(string(a.Type)) < strings.ToLower(string(b.Type))
512			case sortByResponse:
513				less = a.ResponseTime < b.ResponseTime
514			default: // sortByName
515				less = strings.ToLower(a.Name) < strings.ToLower(b.Name)
516			}
517	
518			if m.sortAsc {
519				return less
520			}
521			return !less
522		})
523	
524		return sorted
525	}

cycle through `cycleFocus()`, which skips the locked checkbox. Switching to

### D8 — Write-only CRUD flags and an unreachable handler in the status view

`internal/ui/status/model.go:64-67` and `internal/ui/status/update.go:57-60`

`Model.creating`, `Model.editing` and `Model.confirming` are assigned in five
places and read in none: the view keys off `componentForm != nil` and
`confirmModal != nil` instead. `HasActiveForm`, the one method that read them, is
commented out at `model.go:139`.

`ComponentFormCancelledMsg` is never sent either. `ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg`
answers `esc` by returning a nil form, and the caller stores that — so the
`case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg` branch in `Update()` cannot run. Its
body is the only thing that would reset `creating` / `editing`, which is why they
would stay true after a cancellation if anything did read them.

Harmless today, but it is state that lies: a reader reasonably assumes those
flags mean something. Found while writing the phase 2 tests; the tests
deliberately assert on `componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags,
so removing them breaks nothing.

**Fix:** delete the three fields, the unreachable case and the message type — or
give `esc` a message and make the flags load-bearing. Deleting is the smaller
change and matches how the view already works.

1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 (the byte-vs-rune lot), then D2, D5 and D7, were fixed; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). **D4 is the only one left**, and it is waiting on a decision
16	rather than on work.
17	
18	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
19	
20	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
21	
22	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
23	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
24	
25	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
26	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
27	than a drive-by fix.
28	
29	Note that the surrounding code moved when D2 was fixed: `tab` / `shift+tab` now
30	cycle through `cycleFocus()`, which skips the locked checkbox. Switching to

39	`confirmModal != nil` instead. `HasActiveForm`, the one method that read them, is
40	commented out at `model.go:139`.

43	answers `esc` by returning a nil form, and the caller stores that — so the
44	`case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg` branch in `Update()` cannot run. Its
45	body is the only thing that would reset `creating` / `editing`, which is why they
46	would stay true after a cancellation if anything did read them.
47

56	
57	### 1.1 Fixed
58	
59	**The status view's help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing
60	the phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.
61	
62	`GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while the binding has
63	been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter was missing
64	altogether. The empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too. A test now
65	asserts that every key `GetShortcuts()` advertises appears in the help, so the
66	two cannot drift apart again silently.
67	
68	**D7** (`extractTarGz` kept parent references in archive paths), **D2** (the
69	"permanent delete" checkbox was documented as locked but was not) and **D5** (an
70	unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`) were fixed together — three small,
71	independent defects with no shared code.
72	
73	`extractTarGz` now routes every member name through `sanitizeArchivePath`, which
74	normalises the separators and rejects anything resolving outside the root.
75	Cleaning happens *after* the leading separator is stripped, not before:
76	`path.Clean("/../x")` returns `"/x"`, which would have absorbed the traversal
77	silently instead of exposing it. Traversal that resolves back inside the root
78	(`templates/../README.md`) is kept, normalised. Backslashes are folded to `/`
79	first, so `..\..\etc\passwd` cannot pass as an ordinary filename on a tar reader
80	that treats it as one.
81	
82	The delete modal carries a `locked` flag, set only by
83	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent`. Rather than merely making the toggle a no-op,
84	navigation skips the checkbox entirely (`minFocus()` / `cycleFocus()`) and the
85	line renders dimmed: a focusable control that ignores every key is more
86	confusing than one that is plainly not there.
87	
88	The `CreationForm` clamp was deleted and replaced by a comment recording why it
89	cannot fire, so it is not reintroduced defensively. A test pins the invariant it
90	was guarding.
91	
92	Both self-annulling tests became real assertions:
93	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable` →
94	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsLocked` (plus navigation and
95	confirmation cases), and `TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys` →
96	`TestExtractTarGzRejectsParentTraversal` (table-driven over five escape shapes)
97	alongside `TestExtractTarGzNormalisesContainedTraversal`.
98	
99	**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
100	looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
101	fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.
102	
103	Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
104	`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
105	the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
106	terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
107	ones.
108	
109	A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
110	in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
111	Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is

126	The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
127	credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
128	unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
129	credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the

## No seam needed

The view layer is testable as-is, for the reason `internal/ui/testutil` documents: constructors are pure and `Update()` is a pure function, so feeding synthetic messages fully determines the resulting state.

No test executes a command `Update` returns — `checkComponents` shells out to the network and `tickCmd` sleeps for a second. Assertions are on model state instead. The two paths that must touch disk (`config.Load` after a save, `config.Save`) redirect `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` at a temporary directory, the same trick `internal/credentials` uses; nothing reaches the developer's `~/.devdesk`.

## Covered

- Check lifecycle: results stored, next check scheduled, a failed check that must **not** wipe the last known good table, error clearing
- Tick scheduling across paused / due / already-running
- Refresh controls and interval clamping at both ends
- Tab switching, cursor movement, top/bottom, vim aliases
- The `.` sort cycle (direction then column) and the ▲/▼ column headers
- CRUD through the form and the confirmation modal, including stale indices and an `Original` that no longer matches anything
- Save/delete results, including a reload that fails on an unparseable config
- The filter bar (Rule 136), including that search mode swallows view shortcuts
- Key routing while an overlay or the search input holds focus
- The Rule 124 footer contract: `RenderFooter`'s line count is asserted against `GetFooterHeight` in five states

`getSelectedComponentIndex` is pinned in both directions — through the sort order and on the SSL tab — because it is what edit and delete resolve against, and an off-by-one there acts on the wrong monitor.

Phase 2 démarrée — premier paquet livré : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/12 (CI verte, `test-race` inclus).

| Paquet | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/status` | 0 % | **93,9 %** |
| `internal/ui/status/components` | 0 % | **93,2 %** |
| global | 18,2 % | **22,7 %** |

**Pas de seam nécessaire.** Les constructeurs sont purs et `Update()` est une fonction pure, donc alimenter des messages synthétiques suffit. Aucun test n'exécute une `Cmd` retournée par `Update` — `checkComponents` sort sur le réseau, `tickCmd` dort une seconde ; les assertions portent sur l'état du modèle. Les deux chemins qui touchent le disque (`config.Load` après une sauvegarde, `config.Save`) redirigent `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` vers un dossier temporaire, comme `internal/credentials` — rien n'atteint ton `~/.devdesk`.

Couvert : cycle de check (dont un échec qui ne doit **pas** vider la table), planification des ticks, contrôles de refresh et clamps d'intervalle, navigation, cycle de tri et ses en-têtes ▲/▼, CRUD via formulaire et modale, résultats save/delete avec un reload qui échoue, la filter bar (Rule 136), le routage clavier sous overlay, et le contrat footer Rule 124 — le nombre de lignes de `RenderFooter` est vérifié contre `GetFooterHeight` dans cinq états.

**Deux trouvailles :**
- *Corrigé ici* — l'aide annonçait `n` pour « Add a new monitor » alors que le binding est `ctrl+n` depuis la Rule 111, et `/` n'était pas documenté du tout ; le message d'état vide disait aussi « Press [n] ». Un test vérifie désormais que chaque touche de `GetShortcuts()` figure dans l'aide, pour que les deux ne redivergent pas en silence.
- *Enregistré en D8* — `Model.creating` / `editing` / `confirming` sont écrits à cinq endroits et lus nulle part, et le `case ComponentFormCancelledMsg` est inatteignable (`esc` ferme le formulaire en retournant nil, sans message). Pas corrigé ici : les tests s'appuient volontairement sur `componentForm`/`confirmModal`, donc supprimer ces champs ne cassera rien.

Reste en phase 2 : `containers` (~1 035 lignes), `dashboard` (~920), `gitlab/auth` (~680).

23	// Init initializes the containers view
24	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
25		return tea.Batch(
26			m.spinner.Tick,
27			tickCmd(),
28			fetchContainers(m.showAll),
29		)
30	}
31	
32	// Update handles messages
33	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
34		switch msg := msg.(type) {
35		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
36			m.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
37			return m, nil
38	
39		case tea.KeyMsg:
40			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
41	
42		case spinner.TickMsg:
43			if m.loading || m.logsLoading {
44				var cmd tea.Cmd
45				m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
46				return m, cmd
47			}
48	
49		case RefreshTickMsg:
50			return m, tea.Batch(fetchContainers(m.showAll), fetchMetrics())
51	
52		case ContainersListMsg:
53			return m.handleContainersList(msg)
54	
55		case ContainerMetricsMsg:
56			return m.handleContainerMetrics(msg)
57	
58		case ContainerActionMsg:
59			return m.handleContainerAction(msg)
60	
61		case ContainerLogsLoadedMsg:
62			return m.handleContainerLogsLoaded(msg)
63	
64		case PagerExitMsg:
65			if m.state == stateLogs {
66				// Reload logs on return from follow or external pager
67				m.logsLoading = true
68				return m, tea.Batch(m.spinner.Tick, fetchContainerLogs(m.logsContainerID, m.logsTimestamps))
69			}
70			return m, tea.Batch(tickCmd(), fetchContainers(m.showAll))
71	
72		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
73			return m.handleConfirmYes()
74	
75		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
76			m.confirmModal = nil
77			m.pendingAction = ""
78			return m, nil
79	
80		case ContainerPruneMsg:
81			return m.handlePruneComplete(msg)
82	
83		case ShellWindowOpenedMsg:
84			if msg.Err != nil {
85				log.Printf("ERROR [containers] open shell window: %v", msg.Err)
86				m.errorMsg = "Failed to open terminal — check logs"
87			}
88			return m, nil
89		}
90	
91		// Update table if no modal active and in table state
92		if m.state == stateTable && m.confirmModal == nil && !m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
93			var cmd tea.Cmd
94			m.containerTable, cmd = m.containerTable.Update(msg)
95			m.refreshSelectionStyle()
96			return m, cmd
97		}
98	
99		return m, nil
100	}

102	// handleKeyMsg processes keyboard input with priority chain
103	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
104		// Priority 1: logs view
105		if m.state == stateLogs {
106			return m.handleLogsKeyMsg(msg)
107		}
108	
109		// Priority 2: confirm modal
110		if m.confirmModal != nil {
111			var cmd tea.Cmd
112			m.confirmModal, cmd = m.confirmModal.Update(msg)
113			return m, cmd
114		}
115	
116		// Priority 3: filter input active
117		if m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
118			return m.handleFilterKeyMsg(msg)
119		}
120	
121		// Priority 4: normal mode
122		return m.handleNormalKeyMsg(msg)

368	// openExternalPager launches docker logs in the system pager (fallback for power users)
369	func (m Model) openExternalPager() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

375	
376		var pagerCmd *exec.Cmd

380			script := fmt.Sprintf(`docker logs --tail 500 %s > "%%TEMP%%\devdesk-logs.txt" 2>&1 && more "%%TEMP%%\devdesk-logs.txt"`, m.logsContainerID)
381			pagerCmd = exec.Command("cmd", "/c", script)

390	// handleContainerLogsLoaded processes fetched log content into the logs viewport
391	func (m Model) handleContainerLogsLoaded(msg ContainerLogsLoadedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
392		m.logsLoading = false
393		if msg.Err != nil {
394			log.Printf("ERROR [containers] logs %s: %v", m.logsContainerName, msg.Err)
395			m.logsRawContent = "Failed to load logs — check logs"
396			m.logsViewport.SetContent(m.logsRawContent)
397			return m, nil
398		}
399		// Strip ANSI escape sequences (colors, cursor moves, etc.) then normalize
400		// line endings. Both are needed: systemd emits colored output, and some
401		// containers use \r for progress-bar overwrites — both break the viewport.
402		content := ansi.Strip(msg.Content)
403		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r\n", "\n")
404		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r", "")
405		m.logsRawContent = content
406	
407		m.refreshLogsViewport()
408		m.logsViewport.GotoBottom()
409		return m, nil
410	}

412	// refreshLogsViewport rebuilds the viewport content applying wrap if enabled.
413	func (m *Model) refreshLogsViewport() {
414		if m.logsWrapEnabled {
415			m.logsViewport.SetContent(wrapLines(m.logsRawContent, m.logsViewport.Width))
416			return
417		}
418		m.logsViewport.SetContent(m.logsRawContent)
419	}

421	// wrapLines soft-wraps content so no line exceeds width runes.
422	func wrapLines(content string, width int) string {
423		if width <= 0 {
424			return content
425		}
426		lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
427		out := make([]string, 0, len(lines))
428		for _, line := range lines {
429			runes := []rune(line)
430			if len(runes) <= width {
431				out = append(out, line)
432				continue
433			}
434			for len(runes) > width {
435				out = append(out, string(runes[:width]))
436				runes = runes[width:]
437			}
438			if len(runes) > 0 {
439				out = append(out, string(runes))
440			}
441		}
442		return strings.Join(out, "\n")
443	}

611	// cycleSort cycles through sort options: each column asc then desc, then next column
612	func (m Model) cycleSort() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
613		if m.sortAsc {
614			m.sortAsc = false
615		} else {
616			m.sortAsc = true
617			nextIdx := 0
618			for i, col := range sortableColumns {
619				if col == m.sortColumn {
620					nextIdx = (i + 1) % len(sortableColumns)
621					break
622				}
623			}
624			m.sortColumn = sortableColumns[nextIdx]
625		}
626		m.updateTable()
627		return m, nil
628	}

630	// sortedContainers returns containers sorted by the current sort column
631	func (m *Model) sortedContainers(containers []docker.Container) []docker.Container {
632		sorted := make([]docker.Container, len(containers))
633		copy(sorted, containers)
634	
635		sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
636			a, b := sorted[i], sorted[j]
637	
638			var less bool
639			switch m.sortColumn {
640			case sortByImage:
641				less = strings.ToLower(a.Image) < strings.ToLower(b.Image)
642			case sortByCPU:
643				less = a.CPUPercent < b.CPUPercent
644			case sortByMem:
645				less = a.MemPercent < b.MemPercent
646			case sortByNetRX:
647				less = a.NetRX < b.NetRX
648			case sortByNetTX:
649				less = a.NetTX < b.NetTX
650			case sortByBlockRX:
651				less = a.BlockRX < b.BlockRX
652			case sortByBlockTX:
653				less = a.BlockTX < b.BlockTX
654			case sortByCreated:
655				less = a.CreatedAt < b.CreatedAt
656			default: // sortByName
657				less = strings.ToLower(a.Name) < strings.ToLower(b.Name)
658			}
659	
660			if m.sortAsc {
661				return less
662			}
663			return !less
664		})
665	
666		return sorted
667	}

701	// formatMemUsage parses docker MemUsage "150MiB / 7.776GiB" into compact "150M/8G"
702	func formatMemUsage(memUsage string) string {
703		parts := strings.SplitN(memUsage, "/", 2)
704		if len(parts) != 2 {
705			return memUsage
706		}
707		used := formatMemValue(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
708		total := formatMemValue(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
709		return used + "/" + total
710	}

712	// formatMemValue converts "150MiB" -> "150M", "7.776GiB" -> "8G", "512KiB" -> "512K"
713	func formatMemValue(val string) string {
714		val = strings.TrimSpace(val)
715	
716		// Try each unit suffix
717		for _, suffix := range []struct {
718			docker string
719			short  string
720			isGig  bool
721		}{
722			{"GiB", "G", true},
723			{"MiB", "M", false},
724			{"KiB", "K", false},
725			{"B", "B", false},
726		} {
727			if strings.HasSuffix(val, suffix.docker) {
728				numStr := strings.TrimSuffix(val, suffix.docker)
729				num, err := strconv.ParseFloat(numStr, 64)
730				if err != nil {
731					return val
732				}
733				if suffix.isGig {
734					// Round GiB to nearest integer
735					return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%s", num, suffix.short)
736				}
737				// For MiB/KiB, show integer
738				return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%s", num, suffix.short)
739			}
740		}
741		return val
742	}

744	// relativeTime converts a docker CreatedAt timestamp to a human-readable relative time
745	func relativeTime(createdAt string) string {
746		// Docker format: "2026-02-07 12:14:13 +0100 CET"
747		// Try parsing with timezone name suffix
748		t, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02 15:04:05 -0700 MST", createdAt)
749		if err != nil {
750			// Try without timezone name
751			t, err = time.Parse("2006-01-02 15:04:05 -0700", createdAt)
752			if err != nil {
753				return createdAt
754			}
755		}
756	
757		return theme.TimeAgo(t) // Rule 127
758	}

761	func (m *Model) updateTable() {
762		sorted := m.sortedContainers(m.filteredContainers())
763		rows := make([]table.Row, 0, len(sorted))
764	
765		for _, c := range sorted {
766			cpuStr := "-"
767			memStr := "-"
768			rxStr := "-"
769			txStr := "-"
770			blkRXStr := "-"
771			blkTXStr := "-"
772	
773			if c.State == "running" {
774				cpuStr = fmt.Sprintf("%.1f%%", c.CPUPercent)
775				memStr = formatMemUsage(c.MemUsage)
776	
777				if c.NetIO != "" {
778					rxStr = formatNetBytes(c.NetRX)
779					txStr = formatNetBytes(c.NetTX)
780				}
781				if c.BlockIO != "" {
782					blkRXStr = formatNetBytes(c.BlockRX)
783					blkTXStr = formatNetBytes(c.BlockTX)
784				}
785			}
786	
787			imageWithState := stateIcon(c.State) + " " + c.Image
788	
789			rows = append(rows, table.Row{
790				c.Name,
791				imageWithState,
792				cpuStr,
793				memStr,
794				rxStr,
795				txStr,
796				blkRXStr,
797				blkTXStr,
798				relativeTime(c.CreatedAt),
799				c.Ports,
800			})
801		}
802	
803		// Update column headers with sort indicators
804		cols := m.containerTable.Columns()
805		if len(cols) >= 10 {
806			sortColIndex := map[sortField]int{
807				sortByName:    0,
808				sortByImage:   1,
809				sortByCPU:     2,
810				sortByMem:     3,
811				sortByNetRX:   4,
812				sortByNetTX:   5,
813				sortByBlockRX: 6,
814				sortByBlockTX: 7,
815				sortByCreated: 8,
816			}
817			baseTitles := map[int]string{
818				0: "Name", 1: "Image", 2: "CPU", 3: "Mem",
819				4: "Net RX", 5: "Net TX", 6: "Block RX", 7: "Block TX", 8: "Created",
820			}
821			for idx, title := range baseTitles {
822				cols[idx].Title = title
823			}
824			if idx, ok := sortColIndex[m.sortColumn]; ok {
825				arrow := " ▲"
826				if !m.sortAsc {
827					arrow = " ▼"
828				}
829				cols[idx].Title = baseTitles[idx] + arrow
830			}
831			m.containerTable.SetColumns(cols)
832		}
833	
834		m.containerTable.SetRows(rows)
835		m.refreshSelectionStyle()
836	}
837	
838	// refreshSelectionStyle updates the table selection color to match the currently selected container's state
839	func (m *Model) refreshSelectionStyle() {
840		sorted := m.sortedContainers(m.filteredContainers())
841		cursor := m.containerTable.Cursor()
842		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(sorted) {
843			m.containerTable.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("normal"))
844			return
845		}
846		state := "normal"
847		if s := sorted[cursor].State; s == "exited" || s == "dead" {
848			state = "error"
849		}
850		m.containerTable.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState(state))
851	}

853	// resize adjusts the table and logs viewport dimensions
854	func (m *Model) resize(width, height int) {
