15	// sectionsToLines splits rendered sections into individual lines with background separators
16	func sectionsToLines(sections []string, colWidth int) []string {
17		emptyLine := theme.EmptyLineBg(colWidth)
18		var lines []string
19		for i, s := range sections {
20			lines = append(lines, strings.Split(s, "\n")...)
21			if i < len(sections)-1 {
22				lines = append(lines, emptyLine)
23			}
24		}
25		return lines
26	}
27	
28	// View renders the dashboard as a two-column layout
29	func (m Model) View() string {
30		colWidth := m.columnWidth()
31	
32		// Left column: GitLab, Services, Certificates, Workspaces
33		leftSections := []string{
34			m.renderGitLabSection(colWidth),
35			m.renderServicesSection(colWidth),
36			m.renderCertificatesSection(colWidth),
37			m.renderWorkspacesSection(colWidth),
38		}
39	
40		// Right column: OCI, Containers, Tools
41		rightSections := []string{
42			m.renderOCISection(colWidth),
43			m.renderContainersSection(colWidth),
44			m.renderToolsSection(colWidth),
45		}
46	
47		// Split sections into lines
48		leftLines := sectionsToLines(leftSections, colWidth)
49		rightLines := sectionsToLines(rightSections, colWidth)
50	
51		// Equalize heights
52		emptyLine := theme.EmptyLineBg(colWidth)
53		maxH := len(leftLines)
54		if len(rightLines) > maxH {
55			maxH = len(rightLines)
56		}
57		for len(leftLines) < maxH {
58			leftLines = append(leftLines, emptyLine)
59		}
60		for len(rightLines) < maxH {
61			rightLines = append(rightLines, emptyLine)
62		}
63	
64		// Combine columns line by line (no JoinHorizontal)
65		var rows []string
66		for i := 0; i < maxH; i++ {
67			rows = append(rows, theme.PadWithBg(leftLines[i], colWidth)+theme.PadWithBg(rightLines[i], colWidth))
68		}
69	
70		content := strings.Join(rows, "\n")
71		return lipgloss.Place(m.width, m.height, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Top,
72			lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Padding(1).Render(content),
73			lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground))
74	}

76	// renderGitLabSection renders the GitLab card (without Projects/Groups)
77	func (m Model) renderGitLabSection(width int) string {
78		var b strings.Builder
79	
80		b.WriteString(theme.SubTitleStyle.Render(theme.IconGitlab+" GitLab") + "\n\n")
81	
82		if !m.shared.IsAuthenticated {
83			b.WriteString(theme.DimStyle.Render("Not connected"))
84			b.WriteString("\n")
85			b.WriteString(theme.HelpStyle.Render("Authenticate with :gitlab-auth"))
86			return m.renderSection(b.String(), width)
87		}
88	
89		if m.loadingGitLab {
90			b.WriteString(theme.DimStyle.Render("Loading..."))
91			return m.renderSection(b.String(), width)
92		}
93	
94		if m.shared.CurrentUser != nil {
95			b.WriteString(theme.StatusOKStyle.Render("✓ Connected") + theme.Bg(" as ") + theme.PrimaryColorStyle.Bold(true).Render(m.shared.CurrentUser.Username))
96			b.WriteString("\n\n")
97		}
98	
99		if m.gitlabStats != nil {
100			stats := m.gitlabStats
101			b.WriteString(theme.Bg("Merge Requests:  ") + renderCount(stats.AssignedMRs) + theme.Bg(" assigned, ") + renderCount(stats.ReviewMRs) + theme.Bg(" to review"))
102			b.WriteString("\n")
103			b.WriteString(theme.Bg("Issues:          ") + renderCount(stats.AssignedIssues) + theme.Bg(" assigned"))
104		}
105	
106		b.WriteString("\n")
107	
108		return m.renderSection(b.String(), width)
109	}

98	// loadSavedCredentials tente de charger les credentials depuis config ou storage
99	func (m *Model) loadSavedCredentials() tea.Cmd {
100		return func() tea.Msg {
101			log.Printf("AUTH: loadSavedCredentials() called")
102	
103			// 1. Essayer depuis la config
104			if m.config.GitLab.URL != "" && m.config.GitLab.Token != "" {
105				log.Printf("AUTH: Credentials loaded from config (URL: %s)", m.config.GitLab.URL)
106				return CredentialsLoadedMsg{
107					URL:    m.config.GitLab.URL,
108					Token:  m.config.GitLab.Token,
109					Source: "config",
110				}
111			}
112	
113			// 2. Sinon essayer depuis le storage (credential helper)
114			if m.storage != nil && m.config.GitLab.URL != "" {
115				log.Printf("AUTH: Trying to load token from storage for URL: %s", m.config.GitLab.URL)
116				token, err := m.storage.Load(m.config.GitLab.URL)
117				if err == nil && token != "" {
118					log.Printf("AUTH: Token loaded from storage successfully")
119					return CredentialsLoadedMsg{
120						URL:    m.config.GitLab.URL,
121						Token:  token,
122						Source: "storage",
123					}
124				}
125				if err != nil {
126					log.Printf("AUTH: Failed to load from storage: %v", err)
127				} else {
128					log.Printf("AUTH: No token found in storage")
129				}
130			} else {
131				if m.storage == nil {
132					log.Printf("AUTH: Storage is nil")
133				}
134				if m.config.GitLab.URL == "" {
135					log.Printf("AUTH: No URL in config")
136				}
137			}
138	
139			// Rien trouvé
140			log.Printf("AUTH: No saved credentials found")
141			return CredentialsLoadedMsg{}
142		}
143	}

19	// Update gère les mises à jour
20	func (m *Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
21		var cmd tea.Cmd
22	
23		switch msg := msg.(type) {
24		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
25			m.width = msg.Width
26			m.height = msg.Height
27	
28		case tea.KeyMsg:
29			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
30	
31		case AuthStartMsg:
32			m.authenticating = true
33			return m, m.spinner.Tick
34	
35		case AuthResultMsg:
36			return m.handleAuthResult(msg)
37	
38		case spinner.TickMsg:
39			if m.authenticating {
40				m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
41				return m, cmd
42			}
43	
44		case CredentialsLoadedMsg:
45			return m.handleCredentialsLoaded(msg)
46	
47		case GitLabAuthSuccessMsg:
48			return m.handleGitLabAuthSuccess(msg)
49	
50		case LogoutCompleteMsg:
51			return m.handleLogoutComplete()
52		}
53	
54		return m, nil
55	}
56	
57	// handleKeyMsg traite les entrées clavier
58	func (m *Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
59		if m.authenticating {
60			return m, nil
61		}
62	
63		switch msg.String() {
64		case "down":
65			m.nextField()
66			return m, nil
67	
68		case "up":
69			m.prevField()
70			return m, nil
71	
72		case "enter":
73			return m.handleEnterKey()
74	
75		case " ":
76			return m.handleSpaceKey()
77	
78		case "ctrl+s":
79			m.saveOption = SaveToHelper
80			return m, nil
81	
82		case "ctrl+f":
83			m.saveOption = SaveToConfig
84			return m, nil
85	
86		default:
87			return m.handleInputUpdate(msg)
88		}
89	}
90	
91	// handleEnterKey traite la touche Enter selon le champ actif
92	func (m *Model) handleEnterKey() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
93		if m.authenticated {
94			return m, m.logout()
95		}
96		if m.currentField < 2 {
97			m.nextField()
98			return m, nil
99		}
100		if m.currentField == 2 {
101			m.saveOption = SaveToHelper
102			return m, nil
103		}
104		if m.currentField == 3 {
105			m.saveOption = SaveToConfig
106			return m, nil
107		}
108		m.authenticating = true
109		return m, tea.Batch(m.spinner.Tick, m.authenticate())
110	}
111	
112	// handleSpaceKey traite la touche espace pour les radio buttons
113	func (m *Model) handleSpaceKey() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
114		if m.currentField == 2 {
115			m.saveOption = SaveToHelper
116			return m, nil
117		}
118		if m.currentField == 3 {
119			m.saveOption = SaveToConfig
120			return m, nil
121		}
122		return m, nil
123	}
124	
125	// handleInputUpdate transmet les messages aux inputs actifs
126	func (m *Model) handleInputUpdate(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
127		var cmd tea.Cmd
128		switch m.currentField {
129		case 0:
130			m.urlInput, cmd = m.urlInput.Update(msg)
131		case 1:
132			m.tokenInput, cmd = m.tokenInput.Update(msg)
133		}
134		return m, cmd
135	}
136	
137	// handleAuthResult traite le résultat d'authentification
138	func (m *Model) handleAuthResult(msg AuthResultMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
139		log.Printf("AUTH: AuthResultMsg received (Error: %v, User: %v)", msg.Error, msg.User != nil)
140		m.authenticating = false
141		if msg.Error != nil {
142			log.Printf("AUTH: Authentication failed: %v", msg.Error)
143			m.error = msg.Error.Error()
144			m.success = ""
145			m.warning = ""
146			return m, nil
147		}
148	
149		log.Printf("AUTH: Authentication successful for user: %s", msg.User.Username)
150		m.error = ""
151		m.authenticated = true
152		m.user = msg.User
153		m.success = "✓ Authenticated as " + msg.User.Username
154		m.warning = msg.SaveWarning
155		m.currentField = 0
156		return m, nil
157	}
158	
159	// handleCredentialsLoaded traite les credentials chargés depuis le storage
160	func (m *Model) handleCredentialsLoaded(msg CredentialsLoadedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
161		log.Printf("AUTH: CredentialsLoadedMsg received (URL: %s, Token: %v, Source: %s)",
162			msg.URL, msg.Token != "", msg.Source)
163		if msg.URL != "" && msg.Token != "" {
164			m.urlInput.SetValue(msg.URL)
165			m.tokenInput.SetValue(msg.Token)
166			log.Printf("AUTH: Starting auto-login")
167			m.authenticating = true
168			return m, tea.Batch(m.spinner.Tick, m.authenticate())
169		}
170		log.Printf("AUTH: No credentials to auto-login")
171		return m, nil
172	}
173	
174	// handleGitLabAuthSuccess traite l'authentification réussie venant de app.go
175	func (m *Model) handleGitLabAuthSuccess(msg GitLabAuthSuccessMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
176		m.authenticating = false
177		m.authenticated = true
178		m.user = msg.User
179		m.error = ""
180		m.success = "✓ Already authenticated as " + msg.User.Username
181		m.currentField = 0
182		return m, nil
183	}
184	
185	// handleLogoutComplete réinitialise l'état après logout
186	func (m *Model) handleLogoutComplete() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
187		m.authenticated = false
188		m.user = nil
189		m.currentField = 0
190		m.tokenInput.SetValue("")
191		m.config.GitLab.Token = ""
192		m.error = ""
193		m.warning = ""
194		m.success = "✓ Logged out successfully"
195		m.urlInput.Focus()
196		return m, nil
197	}
198	
199	// nextField passe au champ suivant
200	func (m *Model) nextField() {
201		m.currentField++
202		if m.currentField > 4 {
203			m.currentField = 4
204		}
205	
206		m.updateFocus()
207	}
208	
209	// prevField passe au champ précédent
210	func (m *Model) prevField() {
211		m.currentField--
212		if m.currentField < 0 {
213			m.currentField = 0
214		}
215	
216		m.updateFocus()
217	}
218	
219	// updateFocus met à jour le focus des champs
220	func (m *Model) updateFocus() {
221		switch m.currentField {
222		case 0:
223			m.urlInput.Focus()
224			m.tokenInput.Blur()
225		case 1:
226			m.urlInput.Blur()
227			m.tokenInput.Focus()
228		default:
229			// Champs 2, 3, 4 (checkboxes et button) - pas de textinput
230			m.urlInput.Blur()
231			m.tokenInput.Blur()
232		}
233	}
234	
235	// authenticate lance l'authentification
236	func (m *Model) authenticate() tea.Cmd {
237		url := m.urlInput.Value()
238		token := m.tokenInput.Value()
239	
240		if url == "" || token == "" {
241			m.error = "URL and token are required"
242			return nil
243		}
244	
245		// Copier les données nécessaires AVANT la goroutine (Rule 110)
246		saveToHelper := m.saveOption == SaveToHelper
247		saveToConfig := m.saveOption == SaveToConfig
248		config := m.config
249	
250		// Commande asynchrone
251		return func() tea.Msg {
252			// Créer l'auth
253			auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(m.storage)
254	
255			// Authentifier avec saveToHelper
256			result, err := auth.Authenticate(url, token, saveToHelper)
257			if err != nil {
258				return AuthResultMsg{
259					Client: nil,
260					User:   nil,
261					Error:  err,
262				}
263			}
264	
265			// Préparer la config à sauvegarder (copie, pas modification du modèle!)
266			config.GitLab.URL = url
267			if saveToConfig {
268				config.GitLab.Token = token
269			}
270	
271			// Retourner le message avec les données
272			return AuthResultMsg{
273				Client:       result.Client,
274				User:         result.User,
275				Error:        nil,
276				SaveWarning:  result.SaveWarning,
277				SaveToConfig: saveToConfig,
278				ConfigToSave: config,
279			}
280		}
281	}
282	
283	// logout déconnecte l'utilisateur
284	func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
285		url := m.urlInput.Value()
286		storage := m.storage
287	
288		// Commande asynchrone
289		return func() tea.Msg {
290			// Créer l'auth
291			auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(storage)
292	
293			// Supprimer les credentials du storage
294			_ = auth.Logout(url) // Ignorer l'erreur, on déconnecte quand même
295	
296			// NE PAS modifier m.config ici (Rule 110) - le faire dans Update()
297			// Retourner le message de logout complet
298			return LogoutCompleteMsg{}
299		}
300	}

The view layer needed no seam either, for the reason `internal/ui/testutil`
documents: constructors are pure and `Update()` is a pure function, so feeding
synthetic messages fully determines the resulting state. No test executes a
command Update returns — they shell out to Docker, hit the GitLab API, sleep for
a second or open a browser — so the assertions are on model state instead. The
few places that must touch disk (`config.Load` after a save, `config.Save`)
redirect `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` at a temporary directory, the same trick
`internal/credentials` uses.

Three constraints the phase surfaced, worth knowing before phases 3–5:

- **Colour has to be forced to test styling.** Under `go test` lipgloss detects
  no TTY, falls back to the Ascii profile and strips every escape sequence — so
  any assertion about colour passes whatever the code does. `containers` calls
  `lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.TrueColor)` for the tests that need it and
  restores it afterwards; that is what makes the Rule 122 check (no escape
  sequences in `table.Row` cells) real rather than vacuous. Verified by styling
  a cell on purpose and watching the test fail. `termenv` moved to a direct
  dependency for this.
- **`bubbles/table` keeps its styles unexported**, so `refreshSelectionStyle` is
  asserted by looking for the error-selection escape sequence in the rendered
  table rather than by reading `Styles()`.
- **`sort.Slice` is not stable**, so fixtures must give every sortable column a
  total order or the expected sequences are ambiguous.

Two handlers are deliberately left uncovered in `containers`: `s` and `S` call
`detectShell`, which runs `docker exec` synchronously *inside* `Update`. The
tests drive those keys only in states that return before reaching it. The same
shape appears in `status.reloadConfigAndCheck`, which calls `config.Load()` from
`Update`. Neither is a Rule 110 violation — nothing mutates the model from a
`Cmd` — but I/O in `Update` blocks the event loop and is untestable without a
seam. Worth a look when phase 5 gets to the router.

input.new_string:
**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.

The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while
the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.
The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`
without documenting it at all.

Both are fixed, and each package now asserts that every key `GetShortcuts()`
advertises appears in `GetHelpContent()` — the check that would have caught the
drift when it was introduced. Worth adding to the remaining views as their
phases land.

1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 (the byte-vs-rune lot), then D2, D5 and D7, were fixed; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). **D4 is the only one left**, and it is waiting on a decision
16	rather than on work.
17	
18	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
19	
20	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
21	
22	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
23	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
24	
25	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
26	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
27	than a drive-by fix.
28	
29	Note that the surrounding code moved when D2 was fixed: `tab` / `shift+tab` now
30	cycle through `cycleFocus()`, which skips the locked checkbox. Switching to
31	`↑ / ↓` remains a one-line change to the key names.
32	
33	### D8 — Write-only CRUD flags and an unreachable handler in the status view
34	
35	`internal/ui/status/model.go:64-67` and `internal/ui/status/update.go:57-60`
36	
37	`Model.creating`, `Model.editing` and `Model.confirming` are assigned in five
38	places and read in none: the view keys off `componentForm != nil` and
39	`confirmModal != nil` instead. `HasActiveForm`, the one method that read them, is
40	commented out at `model.go:139`.
41	
42	`ComponentFormCancelledMsg` is never sent either. `ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg`
43	answers `esc` by returning a nil form, and the caller stores that — so the
44	`case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg` branch in `Update()` cannot run. Its
45	body is the only thing that would reset `creating` / `editing`, which is why they
46	would stay true after a cancellation if anything did read them.
47	
48	Harmless today, but it is state that lies: a reader reasonably assumes those
49	flags mean something. Found while writing the phase 2 tests; the tests
50	deliberately assert on `componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags,
51	so removing them breaks nothing.
52

55	change and matches how the view already works.

58	
59	`internal/ui/containers/model.go:140-147`
60

62	name, *descending*. The status view, which has the same cycle-sort mechanism,
63	sets `sortAsc: true` explicitly. The header does show `Name ▼`, so the view is
64	at least honest about it — but nobody chose it, and it disagrees with the other
65	list view in the application.
66	
67	**Fix:** set `sortAsc: true` in `New()`, one line. Left for a deliberate call
68	because it changes what the user sees on open.
69	`TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending` pins the current behaviour and says so.
70	
71	### 1.1 Fixed
72	
73	**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
74	phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.
75	
76	The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while
77	the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
78	was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.
79	The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`
80	without documenting it at all.
81	
82	Both are fixed, and each package now asserts that every key `GetShortcuts()`
83	advertises appears in `GetHelpContent()` — the check that would have caught the
84	drift when it was introduced. Worth adding to the remaining views as their
85	phases land.
86	
87	**D7** (`extractTarGz` kept parent references in archive paths), **D2** (the
88	"permanent delete" checkbox was documented as locked but was not) and **D5** (an
89	unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`) were fixed together — three small,
90	independent defects with no shared code.
91	
92	`extractTarGz` now routes every member name through `sanitizeArchivePath`, which
93	normalises the separators and rejects anything resolving outside the root.
94	Cleaning happens *after* the leading separator is stripped, not before:
95	`path.Clean("/../x")` returns `"/x"`, which would have absorbed the traversal
96	silently instead of exposing it. Traversal that resolves back inside the root
97	(`templates/../README.md`) is kept, normalised. Backslashes are folded to `/`
98	first, so `..\..\etc\passwd` cannot pass as an ordinary filename on a tar reader
99	that treats it as one.
100	
101	The delete modal carries a `locked` flag, set only by
102	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent`. Rather than merely making the toggle a no-op,
103	navigation skips the checkbox entirely (`minFocus()` / `cycleFocus()`) and the
104	line renders dimmed: a focusable control that ignores every key is more
105	confusing than one that is plainly not there.
106	
107	The `CreationForm` clamp was deleted and replaced by a comment recording why it
108	cannot fire, so it is not reintroduced defensively. A test pins the invariant it
109	was guarding.
110	
111	Both self-annulling tests became real assertions:
112	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsStillToggleable` →
113	`TestDeleteConfirmModalPermanentCheckboxIsLocked` (plus navigation and
114	confirmation cases), and `TestExtractTarGzPreservesParentTraversalInKeys` →
115	`TestExtractTarGzRejectsParentTraversal` (table-driven over five escape shapes)
116	alongside `TestExtractTarGzNormalisesContainedTraversal`.
117	
118	**D1** (`ReportModal.View()` emitted invalid UTF-8), **D3** (`wrapInputLines`
119	looped forever when `wrapWidth <= 0`) and **D6** (`wordWrap` measured bytes) were
120	fixed together, since D1 and D6 were the same byte-vs-rune defect.
121	
122	Rather than patch each call site, the truncation logic moved into
123	`internal/ui/theme/text.go` per Rule 117: `StringWidth`, `TruncateWidth` (keeps
124	the head) and `TruncateTailWidth` (keeps the tail, for paths). All three measure
125	terminal columns, so double-width glyphs are handled too, not just multibyte
126	ones.
127	
128	A **fourth site carried the same defect** and was not recorded here: `truncate`
129	in `internal/ui/security/model.go` sliced bytes exactly like D1 and rendered
130	Trivy finding titles. It is now `theme.TruncateWidth` and the local helper is
131	gone.
132	
133	The two pinned tests that `t.Skip()`d became real assertions
134	(`TestReportModalViewKeepsMultibyteRunesIntact`,
135	`TestWordWrapMeasuresColumnsNotBytes`).
136	
137	One call site was deliberately left alone: `truncateResultLine` in
138	`internal/ui/oci_resources/connectivity_form.go` counts runes rather than bytes,
139	so it is correct — merely imprecise on double-width glyphs. Folding it into the
140	theme helpers is a cleanup, not a defect fix.
141	
142	**Context isolation in `GitCredentialStorage` never worked.** Found while
143	planning the coverage work, not previously recorded.
144	
145	The three methods carried the DevDesk context in the `path` field of the git
146	credential protocol (`path=devdesk/context/<name>`). Git discards that field
147	unless `credential.useHttpPath` is set, which is off by default, so every
148	credential was keyed on `protocol://host` alone. Two contexts pointing at the
149	same GitLab host silently overwrote each other, and the last one to authenticate
150	won for all of them. Verified against a real `git credential` store before and
151	after the fix; it affects every helper (GCM, wincred, osxkeychain), since git
152	strips the path before the helper is ever called.
153	
154	**Fix:** pass `-c credential.useHttpPath=true` on each invocation. Scoping it to
155	the call leaves the user's git configuration alone — setting it globally would

**Sur la question de branche** : pas besoin de repasser par `main` quand les changements sont indépendants. Là j'ai fait une seule branche, un commit par paquet, une PR — repasser par `main` n'a d'intérêt que si un changement dépend du précédent (ou si tu veux mergerdans un ordre précis).

**Phase 2 terminée** : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/13 (CI verte, `test-race` inclus)

| Paquet | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/containers` | 0 % | **87,2 %** |
| `internal/ui/dashboard` | 0 % | **81,5 %** |
| `internal/ui/gitlab/auth` | 0 % | **94,5 %** |
| **global** | 18,2 % | **30,8 %** |

Avec `status` (#12), les cinq paquets de la phase 2 sont tous au-dessus de 80 %.

**Le point qui m'a fait revenir en arrière** : sous `go test`, lipgloss ne détecte pas de TTY, retombe sur le profil Ascii et supprime toutes les séquences d'échappement. Le test Rule 122 que j'avais écrit en #12 (« pas d'ANSI dans les cellules ») passait donc **quoi que fasse le code**. Il force maintenant `termenv.TrueColor` le temps du test — vérifié en stylant une cellule exprès pour voir l'échec. Ça permet aussi d'attester `refreshSelectionStyle`, puisque `bubbles` garde ses styles non exportés : le test cherche la séquence de sélection « erreur » dans le rendu.

**Deux trouvailles :**
- *Corrigé* — l'aide de containers annonçait `S` (shell en nouvelle fenêtre) sans le documenter, même dérive que `n`/`ctrl+n` sur status. Chaque paquet vérifie désormais que toute touche de `GetShortcuts()` figure dans `GetHelpContent()`.
- *Enregistré en D9* — `containers.New()` laisse `sortAsc` à sa valeur zéro : la liste s'ouvre triée **Z→A**, alors que status s'ouvre A→Z. L'en-tête affiche bien `Name ▼`, donc la vue est honnête, mais personne ne l'a choisi. Épinglé par un test plutôt que corrigé — ça change ce que tu vois à l'ouverture, c'est ton arbitrage (une ligne).

**Non couvert volontairement** : `s`/`S` dans containers appellent `detectShell`, qui lance `docker exec` **synchrone dans `Update`**. Même forme que `config.Load()` dans `status.reloadConfigAndCheck`. Ce n'est pas une violation de la Rule 110 — rien ne mute le modèle depuis un `Cmd` — mais ça bloque la boucle d'événements et il faut un seam pour tester. Noté au backlog pour la phase 5.

Prochaine étape possible : phase 3 (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`, ~2 470 stmts) — mais trois de ces fichiers dépassent 800 lignes, donc c'est là que la tension « tester avant de découper » du backlog devient réelle.

261	func (pm *PortsModel) killSelected() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
262		idx := pm.table.Cursor()
263		if idx < 0 || idx >= len(pm.filtered) {
264			return pm, nil

267		if entry.PID == "" {

274	func (pm *PortsModel) applyFilters() {
275		pm.filtered = nil
276		query := strings.ToLower(pm.filterBar.SearchQuery())
277		filterTCP := pm.filterBar.IsTokenActive(filterTokenTCP)
278		filterUDP := pm.filterBar.IsTokenActive(filterTokenUDP)
279		filterListen := pm.filterBar.IsTokenActive(filterTokenListen)
280		filterEstab := pm.filterBar.IsTokenActive(filterTokenEstab)
281	
282		for _, p := range pm.ports {
283			// Proto filter (OR logic): skip if no active proto matches.
284			if (filterTCP || filterUDP) &&
285				(!filterTCP || !strings.EqualFold(p.Protocol, filterTokenTCP)) &&
286				(!filterUDP || !strings.EqualFold(p.Protocol, filterTokenUDP)) {
287				continue
288			}
289			// State filter (OR logic): skip if no active state matches.
290			if (filterListen || filterEstab) &&
291				(!filterListen || !strings.EqualFold(p.State, filterTokenListen)) &&
292				(!filterEstab || !strings.EqualFold(p.State, filterTokenEstab)) {
293				continue
294			}
295			if query != "" {
296				haystack := strings.ToLower(p.Protocol + " " + p.State + " " + p.LocalAddr + " " + p.PeerAddr + " " + p.Process + " " + p.PID)
297				if !strings.Contains(haystack, query) {
298					continue
299				}
300			}
301			pm.filtered = append(pm.filtered, p)
302		}
303	}

306	func (pm *PortsModel) tableColumns() []table.Column {
307		w := max(pm.width-2, 30)
308		available := w - 6*2 // 6 columns × 2-char cell padding
309		col1W := 6
310		col2W := 10
311		col3W := 26
312		col4W := 26
313		col5W := 7
314		col6W := max(available-col1W-col2W-col3W-col4W-col5W, 10)
315		return []table.Column{
316			{Title: "Proto", Width: col1W},
317			{Title: "State", Width: col2W},
318			{Title: "Local Address", Width: col3W},
319			{Title: "Peer Address", Width: col4W},
320			{Title: "PID", Width: col5W},
321			{Title: "Process", Width: col6W},
322		}
323	}

327		var rows []table.Row
328		for _, p := range pm.filtered {
329			rows = append(rows, table.Row{p.Protocol, p.State, p.LocalAddr, p.PeerAddr, p.PID, p.Process})
330		}
331		return rows
332	}

334	func (pm *PortsModel) rebuildTable() {
335		if pm.width == 0 {
336			return
337		}
338	
339		pm.filterBar.Resize(max(pm.width, 30))
340	
341		// pm.height IS the viewport content height sent by the app (Rule 124).
342		// Filter bar is rendered in the footer (outside the viewport).
343		tableHeight := pm.height
344		if tableHeight < 3 {
345			tableHeight = 3
346		}
347	
348		rows := pm.buildRows()
349	
350		if !pm.tableReady {
351			// First render: create the table from scratch.
352			t := table.New(
353				table.WithColumns(pm.tableColumns()),
354				table.WithRows(rows),
355				table.WithFocused(true),
356				table.WithHeight(tableHeight),
357			)
358			t.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
359			pm.table = t
360			pm.tableReady = true
361			pm.lastTableWidth = pm.width
362			pm.lastTableHeight = tableHeight
363			return
364		}
365	
366		// Structural change (terminal resize or filter bar toggled): update columns + height.
367		if pm.width != pm.lastTableWidth || tableHeight != pm.lastTableHeight {
368			pm.table.SetColumns(pm.tableColumns())
369			pm.table.SetHeight(tableHeight)
370			pm.lastTableWidth = pm.width
371			pm.lastTableHeight = tableHeight
372		}
373	
374		// Data update: SetRows preserves cursor index and viewport scroll position.
375		pm.table.SetRows(rows)
376	}

1	package netdiag
2	
3	import (
4		"regexp"
5		"strings"
6	
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
10	)
11	
12	// dnsRecord holds one parsed answer record from dig output.
13	type dnsRecord struct {
14		name  string
15		ttl   string
16		rtype string
17		value string
18	}
19	
20	// digResult holds the structured fields extracted from a dig output.
21	type digResult struct {
22		status    string // NOERROR, NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, …
23		question  string // e.g. "google.com. A"
24		answers   []dnsRecord
25		queryTime string // e.g. "2 ms"
26		server    string // e.g. "8.8.8.8#53"
27	}
28	
29	var (
30		reDigStatus    = regexp.MustCompile(`status:\s*(\w+)`)
31		reDigQueryTime = regexp.MustCompile(`;;\s*Query time:\s*(\d+)\s*msec`)
32		reDigServer    = regexp.MustCompile(`;;\s*SERVER:\s*(\S+)`)
33		reDigAnswer    = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\S+)\s+(\d+)\s+IN\s+(\w+)\s+(.+)$`)
34		reDigQuestion  = regexp.MustCompile(`^;\s*(\S+)\s+IN\s+(\w+)`)
35	)
36	
37	// parseDNSOutput extracts structured data from raw dig output.
38	func parseDNSOutput(output string) digResult {
39		var res digResult
40		section := ""
41	
42		for line := range strings.SplitSeq(output, "\n") {
43			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
44	
45			// Section detection
46			switch {
47			case strings.Contains(trimmed, ";; QUESTION SECTION:"):
48				section = "question"
49				continue
50			case strings.Contains(trimmed, ";; ANSWER SECTION:"):
51				section = "answer"
52				continue
53			case strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, ";;") && strings.HasSuffix(trimmed, "SECTION:"):
54				section = "other"
55				continue
56			}
57	
58			// Global metadata
59			if m := reDigStatus.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil && res.status == "" {
60				res.status = m[1]
61			}
62			if m := reDigQueryTime.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil {
63				res.queryTime = m[1] + " ms"
64			}
65			if m := reDigServer.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil {
66				srv := m[1]
67				if idx := strings.Index(srv, "("); idx > 0 {
68					srv = srv[:idx]
69				}
70				res.server = srv
71			}
72	
73			switch section {
74			case "question":
75				if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, ";") && !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, ";;") {
76					if m := reDigQuestion.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil {
77						res.question = strings.TrimSuffix(m[1], ".") + "  " + m[2]
78					}
79				}
80			case "answer":
81				if trimmed == "" || strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, ";") {
82					continue
83				}
84				if m := reDigAnswer.FindStringSubmatch(trimmed); m != nil {
85					value := strings.TrimSpace(m[4])
86					value = strings.TrimSuffix(value, ".")
87					res.answers = append(res.answers, dnsRecord{
88						name:  strings.TrimSuffix(m[1], "."),
89						ttl:   m[2],
90						rtype: m[3],
91						value: value,
92					})
93				}
94			}
95		}
96	
97		return res
98	}
99	
100	// formatDNSOutput renders a parsed dig output into styled, padded lines for the details viewport.
101	// Returns one padded string per display line, ready to join with "\n".
102	func formatDNSOutput(output string, width int) []string {
103		res := parseDNSOutput(output)
104		var lines []string
105	
106		// --- Status ---
107		statusIcon := dnsStatusIcon(res.status, len(res.answers))
108		statusText := res.status
109		if statusText == "" {
110			statusText = "unknown"

110			statusText = "unknown"
111		}
112		statusColor := theme.ColorOK
113		if res.status != "NOERROR" {
114			statusColor = theme.ColorError
115		}
116		statusStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(statusColor).Bold(true)
117		lines = append(lines,
118			theme.PadWithBg(statusIcon+spaceBg()+dimStyle().Render("Status")+spaceBg()+spaceBg()+statusStyle.Render(statusText), width),
119			theme.EmptyLineBg(width),
120		)
121	
122		// --- Query ---
123		if res.question != "" {
124			lines = append(lines,
125				theme.PadWithBg(dnsSectionBullet()+spaceBg()+dimStyle().Render("Query")+spaceBg()+spaceBg()+textStyle().Render(res.question), width),
126				theme.EmptyLineBg(width),
127			)
128		}
129	
130		// --- Answers ---
131		typeStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight)
132		switch {
133		case len(res.answers) > 0:
134			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(dnsSectionBullet()+spaceBg()+dimStyle().Render("Answers"), width))
135			for _, rec := range res.answers {
136				txt := theme.Bg("  ") +
137					textStyle().Render(rec.value) +
138					spaceBg() + spaceBg() +
139					typeStyle.Render(rec.rtype) +
140					spaceBg() + spaceBg() +
141					dimStyle().Render("TTL "+rec.ttl+"s")
142				lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(txt, width))
143			}
144			lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(width))
145		case res.status == "NOERROR":
146			lines = append(lines,
147				theme.PadWithBg(dnsSectionBullet()+spaceBg()+dimStyle().Render("Answers")+spaceBg()+spaceBg()+dimStyle().Render("(none)"), width),
148				theme.EmptyLineBg(width),
149			)
150		}
151	
152		// --- Stats ---
153		if res.queryTime != "" {
154			lines = append(lines,
155				theme.PadWithBg(dnsSectionBullet()+spaceBg()+dimStyle().Render("Query time")+spaceBg()+spaceBg()+textStyle().Render(res.queryTime), width),
156			)
157		}
158		if res.server != "" {
159			lines = append(lines,
160				theme.PadWithBg(dnsSectionBullet()+spaceBg()+dimStyle().Render("Server")+spaceBg()+spaceBg()+textStyle().Render(res.server), width),
161			)
162		}
163	
164		return lines
165	}
166	
167	// dnsStatusIcon returns a colored status icon based on the DNS result.
168	func dnsStatusIcon(status string, answerCount int) string {
169		base := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground)
170		switch {
171		case status == "NOERROR" && answerCount > 0:
172			return base.Foreground(theme.ColorOK).Render(theme.IconOK)
173		case status == "NOERROR" && answerCount == 0:
174			return base.Foreground(theme.ColorWarn).Render(theme.IconWarning)
175		default:
176			return base.Foreground(theme.ColorError).Render(theme.IconError)
177		}
178	}
179	
180	// dnsSectionBullet returns a dimmed bullet used for section labels.
181	func dnsSectionBullet() string {
182		return lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorDim).Render("◆")
183	}

This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.

**The order settled on for phase 3 is: surface tests, then split, then complete
coverage** — per package, so each split has a net under it without the tests
being written against a layout that is about to change. It worked on `netdiag`:
the surface pass reached 58.8 % driving `Update()` and `View()` only, the split
moved five blocks of code with the coverage figure unchanged to the statement,
and the completion pass took it to 86.1 %. The discipline that makes it work is
asserting on behaviour rather than on internals — no test named a file, and the
only ones that reach into the model do so for state the view has no other way to
expose.

1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 (the byte-vs-rune lot), then D2, D5 and D7, were fixed; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). **D4 is the only one left**, and it is waiting on a decision
16	rather than on work.
17	
18	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
19	
20	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
21	
22	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
23	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
24	
25	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
26	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
27	than a drive-by fix.
28	
29	Note that the surrounding code moved when D2 was fixed: `tab` / `shift+tab` now
30	cycle through `cycleFocus()`, which skips the locked checkbox. Switching to
31	`↑ / ↓` remains a one-line change to the key names.
32	
33	### D8 — Write-only CRUD flags and an unreachable handler in the status view
34	
35	`internal/ui/status/model.go:64-67` and `internal/ui/status/update.go:57-60`
36	
37	`Model.creating`, `Model.editing` and `Model.confirming` are assigned in five
38	places and read in none: the view keys off `componentForm != nil` and
39	`confirmModal != nil` instead. `HasActiveForm`, the one method that read them, is
40	commented out at `model.go:139`.
41	
42	`ComponentFormCancelledMsg` is never sent either. `ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg`
43	answers `esc` by returning a nil form, and the caller stores that — so the
44	`case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg` branch in `Update()` cannot run. Its
45	body is the only thing that would reset `creating` / `editing`, which is why they
46	would stay true after a cancellation if anything did read them.
47	
48	Harmless today, but it is state that lies: a reader reasonably assumes those
49	flags mean something. Found while writing the phase 2 tests; the tests
50	deliberately assert on `componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags,
51	so removing them breaks nothing.
52	
53	**Fix:** delete the three fields, the unreachable case and the message type — or
54	give `esc` a message and make the flags load-bearing. Deleting is the smaller
55	change and matches how the view already works.
56	
57	### D9 — The containers list opens sorted Z→A
58	
59	`internal/ui/containers/model.go:140-147`
60	
61	`New()` sets neither `sortColumn` nor `sortAsc`, so both take their zero value:
62	name, *descending*. The status view, which has the same cycle-sort mechanism,
63	sets `sortAsc: true` explicitly. The header does show `Name ▼`, so the view is
64	at least honest about it — but nobody chose it, and it disagrees with the other
65	list view in the application.
66	
67	**Fix:** set `sortAsc: true` in `New()`, one line. Left for a deliberate call
68	because it changes what the user sees on open.
69	`TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending` pins the current behaviour and says so.
70	
71	### 1.1 Fixed
72	
73	**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
74	phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.
75	
76	The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while
77	the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
78	was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.
79	The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`
80	without documenting it at all.
81	
82	Both are fixed, and each package now asserts that every key `GetShortcuts()`
83	advertises appears in `GetHelpContent()` — the check that would have caught the
84	drift when it was introduced. Worth adding to the remaining views as their
85	phases land.
86	
87	**D7** (`extractTarGz` kept parent references in archive paths), **D2** (the
88	"permanent delete" checkbox was documented as locked but was not) and **D5** (an
89	unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`) were fixed together — three small,
90	independent defects with no shared code.
91	
92	`extractTarGz` now routes every member name through `sanitizeArchivePath`, which
93	normalises the separators and rejects anything resolving outside the root.
94	Cleaning happens *after* the leading separator is stripped, not before:
95	`path.Clean("/../x")` returns `"/x"`, which would have absorbed the traversal
96	silently instead of exposing it. Traversal that resolves back inside the root
97	(`templates/../README.md`) is kept, normalised. Backslashes are folded to `/`
98	first, so `..\..\etc\passwd` cannot pass as an ordinary filename on a tar reader
99	that treats it as one.
100	
101	The delete modal carries a `locked` flag, set only by
102	`NewDeleteConfirmModalPermanent`. Rather than merely making the toggle a no-op,
103	navigation skips the checkbox entirely (`minFocus()` / `cycleFocus()`) and the

Phase 3 démarrée sur `netdiag`, en trois étapes comme convenu : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/14 (CI verte)

| | Couverture | `model.go` |
|---|---|---|
| avant | 15,9 % | 1114 lignes |
| après étape 1 (tests de surface) | **58,9 %** | 1114 |
| après étape 2 (découpe) | **58,9 %** | **172** |
| après étape 3 (complément) | **86,1 %** | 172 |
| global dépôt | 30,8 % → **37,7 %** | |

**La ligne du milieu est le résultat qui compte** : couverture identique au statement près avant et après la découpe. L'étape 1 ne pilote que `Update()` et `View()` — aucun test ne nomme un fichier ni un helper — donc déplacer cinq blocs de code leur est invisible. C'est la preuve que l'ordre tient, et la raison de le garder pour les trois paquets restants.

Un commit par étape, donc celui du milieu est vérifiable isolément (`git show 1ab6855` = déplacement pur, aucune signature ni comportement modifié). `model.go` passe de 1114 à 172 lignes, réparties en `validation.go` (97, qui rejoint le `validation_test.go` déjà présent), `run.go` (125), `view.go` (214), `header.go` (233), `update.go` (314).

**Une trouvaille, corrigée** : `firstOutputLine` faisait `line[:maxLen-3]` pour remplir la colonne Output de la table de résultats — un diagnostic dont la première ligne contient une rune multi-octets était coupé en plein milieu. Même défaut que D1/D6, et dans une **cellule de table**, donc ça bave sur toutes les lignes en dessous (Rule 122). C'est le **cinquième** site de ce défaut ; le backlog note maintenant de grepper le slicing de strings au fil des phases restantes.

Deux points de l'étape 3 qui méritent ton œil : les filtres de l'onglet Ports (OR *dans* un groupe, AND *entre* groupes) et les deux règles de curseur volontairement différentes — un refresh de données préserve le curseur (poll toutes les 2 s, sinon tu es renvoyé en haut en permanence), un changement de filtre le remet à zéro (les lignes en dessous ont bougé).

Reste en phase 3, par taille croissante : `workspaces` (1299), `explorer` (1402), `security` (1977).

test: cover the workspaces view through Update and View (phase 3, step 1)

Second package of phase 3, same three-step order. internal/ui/workspaces goes
0% -> 60.3% driving Update() and View() only, since model.go is 1299 lines and
the split follows in the next commit.

Covered: the drill-down navigation and its cursor stack (going back restores
the cursor the user left at, one level per pop), selection mode — where enter
confirms the directory being *browsed* rather than the highlighted row, and esc
backs out one level before cancelling — the create/rename/delete flows with
their stale-index guards, and the Rule 126 scan cache semantics: ctrl+s purges
one repo, A skips what is already cached, ctrl+a purges everything.

Also the pure helpers, which had no coverage at all: extractRemotePath and
normalizeRemoteURL over both URL syntaxes (the latter is asserted to strip
credentials, since the result is handed to a browser), detectProjectType's
signature ordering, and detectSubRepoPaths against a real temp tree including
a repo nested inside another repo, a hidden directory and the depth limit.

One finding, fixed here: bubbles/table.SetRows does not clamp the cursor when
the row count shrinks. Drilling into a directory with fewer entries — or
narrowing the filter — left the cursor past the end, so nothing was highlighted
and enter, ctrl+d, r and ctrl+s all silently did nothing until the user pressed
an arrow key. updateTableData now clamps. The containers view avoids this by
calling GotoTop() after every filter change; this one had no equivalent.
EOF

Rule 124 footer contract across six states including selection mode.

Shortcuts get the most attention here, because this view has the most
state-dependent list in the app and the backlog documents which key appears
when: enter only for a scanned repo, ctrl+w only for a git repo, ctrl+s for a
repo or a directory holding repos, ctrl+n hidden when a repo is selected. Four
selections, each asserted for what must be present *and* absent.

WorkspaceInput: focus cycling, enter submitting from both the field and the
button, blank names rejected, and the rename variant emitting its own message.

The filesystem commands are executed rather than asserted on identity — they
touch nothing but a temp directory. That covers createWorkspace (including the
first-run root creation and the browsed-subdirectory case), deleteEntry,
renameEntry, loadEntries (hidden entries skipped, a missing root created, a
vanished subdirectory reported) and enrichEntry against a throwaway git
repository, which is what proves the branch, remote and dirty-tree counters are
read correctly. It skips when git is not on PATH, like internal/gitlab does.

One finding, fixed: the help advertised `n` and `Enter` where the bindings are
`ctrl+n` and `enter`, and `/` was undocumented — the third view with this
drift. The empty-state hint said "Press [n]" too. The check that catches it is
now in this package as well.

2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there

12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 (the byte-vs-rune lot), then D2, D5 and D7, were fixed; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). **D4 is the only one left**, and it is waiting on a decision
16	rather than on work.
17	
18	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
19	
20	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
21	
22	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
23	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
24	
25	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
26	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
27	than a drive-by fix.
28	
29	Note that the surrounding code moved when D2 was fixed: `tab` / `shift+tab` now
30	cycle through `cycleFocus()`, which skips the locked checkbox. Switching to
31	`↑ / ↓` remains a one-line change to the key names.
32	
33	### D8 — Write-only CRUD flags and an unreachable handler in the status view
34	
35	`internal/ui/status/model.go:64-67` and `internal/ui/status/update.go:57-60`
36	
37	`Model.creating`, `Model.editing` and `Model.confirming` are assigned in five
38	places and read in none: the view keys off `componentForm != nil` and
39	`confirmModal != nil` instead. `HasActiveForm`, the one method that read them, is
40	commented out at `model.go:139`.
41	
42	`ComponentFormCancelledMsg` is never sent either. `ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg`
43	answers `esc` by returning a nil form, and the caller stores that — so the
44	`case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg` branch in `Update()` cannot run. Its
45	body is the only thing that would reset `creating` / `editing`, which is why they
46	would stay true after a cancellation if anything did read them.
47	
48	Harmless today, but it is state that lies: a reader reasonably assumes those
49	flags mean something. Found while writing the phase 2 tests; the tests
50	deliberately assert on `componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags,
51	so removing them breaks nothing.
52	
53	**Fix:** delete the three fields, the unreachable case and the message type — or
54	give `esc` a message and make the flags load-bearing. Deleting is the smaller
55	change and matches how the view already works.
56

58	
59	`internal/ui/containers/model.go:140-147`
60	
61	`New()` sets neither `sortColumn` nor `sortAsc`, so both take their zero value:
62	name, *descending*. The status view, which has the same cycle-sort mechanism,
63	sets `sortAsc: true` explicitly. The header does show `Name ▼`, so the view is
64	at least honest about it — but nobody chose it, and it disagrees with the other
65	list view in the application.
66	
67	**Fix:** set `sortAsc: true` in `New()`, one line. Left for a deliberate call
68	because it changes what the user sees on open.
69	`TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending` pins the current behaviour and says so.

72	
73	**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
74	phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.

77	the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
78	was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.

## New technique: execute the filesystem commands

`createWorkspace`, `deleteEntry`, `renameEntry`, `loadEntries` and `enrichEntry` touch nothing but a temp directory, so the tests **run** them instead of asserting on command identity. `enrichEntry` runs against a throwaway git repository — that is what proves the branch, remote and dirty-tree counters are actually read correctly; a stub would only prove the stub works. It skips when `git` is not on `PATH`, like `internal/gitlab` does.

Only the Docker- and desktop-backed commands (scans, IDE, terminal, browser) are left alone.

## Two findings

**Fixed — a stranded cursor.** `bubbles/table.SetRows` does not clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks. Drilling into a directory with fewer entries, or narrowing the filter, left the cursor past the end: nothing highlighted, and `enter`, `ctrl+d`, `r`, `ctrl+s` all silently did nothing until you pressed an arrow key. `updateTableData` now clamps. The containers view avoids this by calling `GotoTop()` after every filter change; this one had no equivalent — worth checking `explorer`, which has the same drill-down shape.

**Fixed — help drift, third instance.** Documented `n` and `Enter` where the bindings are `ctrl+n` and `enter`, `/` undocumented, and the same stale "Press [n]" in the empty state. Status (#12) and containers (#13) had the same thing. Three in a row, so assume `explorer` and `security` do too.

## Worth reviewing

- **Selection mode**: `enter` confirms the directory being *browsed*, not the highlighted row — the user drills in with `→` first. Getting that backwards scans the wrong tree, so it is pinned both ways, along with `esc` backing out one level before it cancels.
- **Rule 126 scan semantics**: `ctrl+s` purges one repo's cache entry, `A` skips what is already cached, `ctrl+a` purges everything. All three asserted against the cache directly.
- **Rule 130 shortcuts**: this view has the most state-dependent list in the app. Four selections (scanned repo, unscanned repo, directory with nested repos, plain directory), each asserted for what must be present *and* absent.
- **Cursor stack**: going back restores the cursor the user left at, one level per pop.

## Test plan

- [x] `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues
- [x] `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`
- [x] Coverage measured at each step; step 2 verified behaviour-neutral
- [ ] `mise run test-race` — runs in CI
EOF

J'ai mergé #14 puis enchaîné sur `workspaces` — deuxième paquet de la phase 3 : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/15 (CI verte)

| | Couverture | `model.go` |
|---|---|---|
| avant | 0 % | 1299 lignes |
| étape 1 (tests de surface) | **60,3 %** | 1299 |
| étape 2 (découpe) | **60,3 %** | **129** |
| étape 3 (complément) | **81,3 %** | 129 |
| global | 37,7 % → **43,6 %** | |

Même vérification qu'avec netdiag : la découpe ne bouge pas la couverture d'un statement (`git show 946bda9` — déplacement pur, seuls les blocs d'import diffèrent).

**Une technique nouvelle qui vaut d'être reprise** : les commandes qui ne touchent qu'au système de fichiers (`createWorkspace`, `deleteEntry`, `renameEntry`, `loadEntries`, `enrichEntry`) sont **exécutées** contre `t.TempDir()` plutôt qu'assertées sur leur identité. `enrichEntry` tourne contre un vrai dépôt git jetable — c'est ce qui prouve que la branche, le remote et les compteurs de l'arbre sale sont bien lus ; un stub ne prouverait que le stub. Skip si `git` n'est pas sur le `PATH`, comme `internal/gitlab`.

**Deux trouvailles, corrigées :**
- **Curseur bloqué** — `bubbles/table.SetRows` ne clampe pas le curseur quand le nombre de lignes diminue. En descendant dans un dossier plus petit (ou en resserrant le filtre), le curseur restait au-delà de la fin : plus rien de surligné, et `enter`, `ctrl+d`, `r`, `ctrl+s` ne faisaient plus rien jusqu'à ce que tu presses une flèche. Le paquet containers évitait ça avec un `GotoTop()` après chaque filtre ; workspaces n'avait pas l'équivalent. À vérifier dans `explorer`, qui a la même forme de drill-down.
- **Dérive de l'aide, troisième instance** — `n` et `Enter` documentés là où les bindings sont `ctrl+n` et `enter`, `/` absent, et le même « Press [n] » périmé dans l'état vide. Status (#12) et containers (#13) avaient la même chose. Trois vues d'affilée : je pars du principe qu'`explorer` et `security` l'ont aussi.

Points qui méritent ton œil : le mode sélection (`enter` valide le dossier **parcouru**, pas la ligne surlignée — se tromper scanne le mauvais arbre, donc c'est épinglé dans les deux sens) et les sémantiques de cache Rule 126 (`ctrl+s` purge un dépôt, `A` saute ce qui est déjà en cache, `ctrl+a` purge tout).

Reste en phase 3 : `explorer` (1402) et `security` (1977).

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   The user asked me to work the DevDesk backlog (`docs/backlog.md`) task by task, in French, across several turns:
   - `"regarde le backlog pour la prochaine tâche"` — identify the next task from the backlog.
   - After choosing option 1 of my AskUserQuestion: fix the three self-contained defects D7, D2, D5.
   - `"merge"` — merge the resulting PR.
   - `"on commence la couverture phase 2"` — start phase 2 of the coverage plan (status, containers, dashboard, gitlab/auth).
   - `"merge avant de continuer"` — merge before continuing (established as the working rhythm).
   - `"enchaine, est-ce qu'il faut repasser par main à chaque fois ou on peut tout faire dans la même branche"` — continue, and answer whether each package needs its own branch. I answered: no, independent changes go on one branch with one commit per package.
   - `"ok pour le 3"` — approved **option 3** for phase 3: **per package, surface tests → split → complete coverage**, starting with the smallest package (`netdiag`).
   - `"continue"` — continue phase 3 (this led to `workspaces`).

   Overarching intent: raise test coverage toward the agreed 80 % target, split files over the project's 800-line ceiling without freezing their structure with tests, and record every finding in `docs/backlog.md`.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Go + Bubble Tea (Elm architecture): `Init`/`Update`/`View`, `tea.Cmd`, `tea.Msg`, pointer vs value receivers on `Model`.
   - `internal/ui/testutil` harness: `Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Resize`, `Msg`, `Msgs`, `MsgOf[T]` — builds messages and drains commands, never spins a `tea.Program`.
   - Testing doctrine established here: **never execute a Cmd that shells out** (Docker, network, GitLab API, browser, `tea.Tick`); assert on model state instead. **Do** execute filesystem-only Cmds against `t.TempDir()`.
   - `lipgloss` colour profile: degrades to Ascii without a TTY under `go test`, making colour/ANSI assertions vacuous. Fix: `lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.TrueColor)` + restore in `t.Cleanup`. Made `termenv` a direct dependency.
   - `bubbles/table` quirks: `Styles()` is unexported; `SetHeight(h)` subtracts the header so `Height()` returns `h-1`; `SetCursor` clamps to `len-1` (so `-1` on empty); **`SetRows` does NOT clamp the cursor when rows shrink**.
   - `sort.Slice` is not stable → fixtures must give every sortable column a total order.
   - Redirecting `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` to `t.TempDir()` to steer `config.Load`/`config.Save` and `os.UserHomeDir()`.
   - Project rules referenced throughout: 110 (no model mutation in a Cmd), 111 (standard keybindings), 114 (help must be kept in sync), 115 (lipgloss background/no JoinHorizontal), 117 (centralised `theme.*` helpers), 122 (plain text only in `table.Row`), 124 (footer height contract), 126 (scan cache semantics), 127 (`theme.TimeAgo`), 128 (footer message + 3 s clear timer), 129 (English US UI/logs), 130 (dynamic shortcuts), 132/135 (strict key assignment), 136 (`components.FilterBar`), 137 (capitalised imperative shortcut descriptions).
   - Git workflow (from CLAUDE.md, **must be preserved**): never push directly to `main` — the Entire mirror rejects it (`[remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)`). Always `git switch -c <branch>` → `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create --base main --head <branch>` → `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`. `origin` = `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk`, `github` = source of truth. Semantic search (`entire search`) is unavailable in the EU region.
   - Toolchain: `mise run fmt` (go fmt only, no goimports), `mise run lint` (golangci-lint, must be 0 issues), `mise run test-race` (needs cgo/a C compiler — **unavailable locally**, runs in CI on ubuntu-latest).

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`docs/backlog.md`** — the source of truth for tasks; updated in every PR. Now records: D4, D8, D9 open; §1.1 Fixed with D1/D2/D3/D5/D6/D7, the credential-isolation fix, five byte-vs-rune sites, three help-drift instances, the stranded cursor; coverage phase table (phase 0/1 done, 2 done, 3 in progress); the over-800-lines table (5 files left); the phase-3 order and its evidence.

   - **`internal/oci/oci.go`** — D7 fix:
     ```go
     func sanitizeArchivePath(name string) (string, error) {
         clean := strings.ReplaceAll(name, `\`, "/")
         // Drop the leading separator *before* cleaning: path.Clean("/../x") returns
         // "/x", which would silently absorb the traversal instead of exposing it.
         clean = path.Clean(strings.TrimLeft(clean, "/"))
         if clean == "" || clean == "." {
             return "", fmt.Errorf("archive contains an entry with an empty path: %q", name)
         }
         if clean == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") {
             return "", fmt.Errorf("archive entry escapes the root: %q", name)
         }
         return clean, nil
     }
     ```

   - **`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go`** — D2 fix: added `locked bool`, plus
     ```go
     func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) minFocus() int { if m.locked { return 1 }; return 0 }
     func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) cycleFocus(step int) int {
         min := m.minFocus(); span := 3 - min
         return min + ((m.focused-min+step)%span+span)%span
     }
     func (m *DeleteConfirmModal) toggleCheckbox() { if m.locked { return }; m.permanentlyRemove = !m.permanentlyRemove }
     ```
     Rendering dims the checkbox when locked.

   - **`internal/ui/status/view.go`** — help drift fix: `n` → `ctrl+n`, added `/` entry, empty state `Press [ctrl+n]`.
   - **`internal/ui/containers/view.go`** — added the missing `S` help entry.
   - **`internal/ui/workspaces/view.go`** — `n` → `ctrl+n`, `Enter` → `enter`, added `/`, empty state `Press [ctrl+n]`.

   - **`internal/ui/containers/containers_test.go`** — the colour-profile helpers now reused elsewhere:
     ```go
     func withTrueColor(t *testing.T) {
         t.Helper()
         previous := lipgloss.ColorProfile()
         lipgloss.SetColorProfile(termenv.TrueColor)
         t.Cleanup(func() { lipgloss.SetColorProfile(previous) })
     }
     func ansiPrefix(s string) string {
         if !strings.HasPrefix(s, "\x1b[") { return "" }
         end := strings.Index(s, "m"); if end < 0 { return "" }
         return s[:end+1]
     }
     ```

   - **`internal/ui/netdiag/model.go`** → split into `validation.go` (97), `run.go` (125), `model.go` (172), `view.go` (214), `header.go` (233), `update.go` (314). The fifth byte-slicing fix lives in `view.go` now:
     ```go
     func firstOutputLine(output string, maxLen int) string {
         for line := range strings.SplitSeq(output, "\n") {
             line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
             if line != "" { return theme.TruncateWidth(line, maxLen) }
         }
         return ""
     }
     ```

   - **`internal/ui/workspaces/model.go`** → split into `messages.go` (97), `model.go` (129), `table.go` (130), `entry.go` (188), `actions.go` (357), `update.go` (450). The stranded-cursor fix is in `table.go`'s `updateTableData`:
     ```go
     m.table.SetRows(rows)

     // bubbles does not clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks, so drilling
     // into a smaller directory — or narrowing the filter — would leave it past
     // the end. Nothing is highlighted then, and every action that resolves the
     // selection (enter, ctrl+d, r, ctrl+s) silently does nothing.
     if m.table.Cursor() >= len(rows) {
         m.table.SetCursor(max(len(rows)-1, 0))
     }
     ```

   - New test files created: `internal/oci/oci_test.go` (rewritten pinned tests), `internal/ui/components/{delete_confirm_modal,creation_form}_test.go` (edits), `internal/ui/status/{status,update,view}_test.go`, `internal/ui/status/components/component_form_test.go`, `internal/ui/containers/{containers,update,view}_test.go`, `internal/ui/dashboard/{dashboard,view}_test.go`, `internal/ui/gitlab/auth/{auth,view}_test.go`, `internal/ui/netdiag/{netdiag,model,view,ports_model,topology_model,dns_formatter}_test.go`, `internal/ui/workspaces/{workspaces,model,view,input,entry}_test.go`.

4. **Errors and fixes:**

   - **`path.Clean("/" + s)` absorbed the traversal** — my first D7 implementation could never reject `../../etc/passwd`. Fixed by stripping leading separators *before* cleaning.
   - **`%q` escaping broke an error-message assertion** (backslash case) — compared against `fmt.Sprintf("%q", tc.entry)` instead of the raw string; added the `fmt` import.
   - **`SetCursor(99)` clamps** — my "out of range cursor returns -1" test was impossible; reframed as a table/`m.components` desync plus a "no matching config entry" case.
   - **`config.Load()` returns `Default()` for a missing file** — wrote malformed YAML to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` under a redirected HOME to force a real failure.
   - **`table.SetHeight(1)` yields `Height() == 0`** — reframed the assertion to "never negative".
   - **`ctrl+n` / `z` swallowed by an active search box** — correct behaviour; my tests were wrong. Reframed one into `TestSearchModeSwallowsViewShortcuts`; added an `enter` to confirm the search before pressing `z`.
   - **Vacuous Rule 122 tests** — proved empirically that lipgloss strips all escapes under `go test`, then forced `termenv.TrueColor` and *verified the test now fails* by deliberately styling a cell. Retro-fixed the already-merged status version.
   - **`bubbles/table.Styles()` is unexported** — asserted the selection style through the rendered output's ANSI prefix instead.
   - **`sort.Slice` ties** — fixtures gave every sortable column a total order (two rounds of fixes).
   - **Default sort was descending in containers** — my expectations were wrong; discovered `sortAsc` is left at its zero value. Recorded as D9, pinned by `TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending`, and split the helper into `rawModel` / `loadedModel`.
   - **Broken intermediate commit (netdiag step 1)** — I staged the split `model.go` without the new files, producing a non-compiling tree. Fixed by `git reset --soft HEAD~1`, moving the new files to `/tmp/ndsplit`, `git checkout model.go`, re-applying only the `firstOutputLine` fix, verifying the tree standalone, then restoring the split for step 2. Also moved `TestSubModelsDeclareNoEditMode` out of `view_test.go` into `topology_model_test.go` because it depended on a step-3 helper.
   - **`loadEntries` semantics backwards** — a missing workspaces *root* is created on first run; only a missing *browsed* subdirectory errors. Split into two tests plus a hidden-entries test.
   - **Manual import fixing after splits** — `mise run fmt` runs `go fmt`, not goimports, so each extracted file's import block had to be written by hand and iterated against `go build`.

5. **Problem Solving:**
   - Resolved the backlog's own stated tension ("writing tests before splitting freezes the structure") by proving a three-step order works: the surface pass drives only `Update()`/`View()`, so the split moves code with coverage **identical to the statement** (58.8 % → 58.8 % for netdiag; 60.3 % → 60.3 % for workspaces).
   - Established that the view layer needs no seam: pure constructors + pure `Update()` means synthetic messages fully determine state.
   - Found and fixed six real defects across the work (Zip Slip, unlocked "permanent" checkbox, dead clamp, fifth byte-slicing site, stranded cursor, three help-drift instances) and recorded three more for the user's decision (D4, D8, D9).
   - Noted for phase 5: `detectShell` (containers) and `config.Load()` (status) perform I/O **inside `Update`** — not Rule 110 violations, but they block the event loop and need a seam.

6. **All user messages:**
   - "regarde le backlog pour la prochaine tâche"
   - (AskUserQuestion answer) "Défauts D7 + D2 + D5 (recommandé)"
   - "merge"
   - "on commence la couverture phase 2"
   - "merge avant de continuer"
   - "enchaine, est-ce qu'il faut repasser par main à chaque fois ou on peut tout faire dans la même branche"
   - "merge avant de continuer"
   - "ok pour le 3"
   - "continue"

7. **Pending Tasks:**
   - **Merge PR #15** (workspaces) — CI is green, not yet merged.
   - **Finish phase 3**: `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer` (model.go 1402 lines) and `internal/ui/security` (model.go 1977 lines), each through the same three steps.
   - Then phases 4 (`ui/oci_resources`, ~1 995 stmts), 5 (`app`, `scan`, `docker` router/I-O seams), 6 (remainder to 80 %).
   - Awaiting the user's decisions on **D4** (Tab → ↑/↓ in `DeleteConfirmModal`), **D8** (delete the write-only CRUD flags), **D9** (`sortAsc: true` in `containers.New()`).

8. **Current Work:**

   I had just finished the second package of phase 3, `internal/ui/workspaces`, and opened **PR #15** — <https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/15> — titled *"test: cover and split workspaces (phase 3, second package)"*, on branch `test/coverage-phase3-workspaces`. Four commits:
   - `e8f70df` step 1: surface tests, 0 % → 60.3 %, plus the stranded-cursor fix in `updateTableData`.
   - `946bda9` step 2: split `model.go` 1299 → 129 lines into six files, coverage unchanged at 60.3 %.
   - `f83044f` step 3: view/input/filesystem tests, 60.3 % → 81.3 %, plus the third help-drift fix.
   - `6043ad6` docs: backlog update (overall 37.7 % → 43.6 %, phase 3 half done, both findings recorded).

   The very last action was `gh pr checks 15 --watch`, which returned:
   ```
   Lint and build	pass	1m8s
   Test	pass	2m0s
   ```
   So CI is green and PR #15 is ready to merge. I had not yet reported this result to the user.

9. **Optional Next Step:**

   Report the PR #15 result to the user (in French, as throughout), then — consistent with the established rhythm where the user said `"merge avant de continuer"` before each new package — merge PR #15 and start the third package of phase 3, `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer`, using the same three steps the user approved with `"ok pour le 3"`.

   The order is recorded verbatim in the backlog commit I just made: *"the per-package order settled for phase 3: surface tests, then split, then complete coverage"*, and my last report to the user stated: *"Reste en phase 3, par taille croissante : `workspaces` (1299), `explorer` (1402), `security` (1977)."* — with `workspaces` now done, `explorer` is next.

   The backlog also flags two things to check specifically in `explorer`: *"Three views in a row carried it, so assume `explorer` and `security` do as well"* (help drift) and *"Worth checking in `explorer`, which has the same drill-down shape"* (the stranded cursor).
