1	// Package testutil provides helpers for driving Bubble Tea models in tests.
2	//
3	// The views in this project are testable without a terminal because of two
4	// properties the codebase already guarantees:
5	//
6	//   - Constructors are pure. New(cfg) performs no I/O; Docker and network calls
7	//     are issued from Init() as tea.Cmd values.
8	//   - Update() is a pure function (Model, Msg) -> (Model, Cmd). Rule 110 forbids
9	//     mutating the model inside a Cmd, so feeding synthetic messages to Update()
10	//     fully determines the resulting state.
11	//
12	// These helpers therefore build messages and drain commands; they never spin up
13	// a tea.Program.
14	package testutil
15	
16	import (
17		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
18	)
19	
20	// namedKeys maps the key names used throughout the views (they all dispatch on
21	// tea.KeyMsg.String()) onto the key types that render back to those names.
22	var namedKeys = map[string]tea.KeyType{
23		"enter":     tea.KeyEnter,
24		"esc":       tea.KeyEsc,
25		"escape":    tea.KeyEscape,
26		"up":        tea.KeyUp,
27		"down":      tea.KeyDown,
28		"left":      tea.KeyLeft,
29		"right":     tea.KeyRight,
30		"tab":       tea.KeyTab,
31		"shift+tab": tea.KeyShiftTab,
32		" ":         tea.KeySpace,
33		"space":     tea.KeySpace,
34		"backspace": tea.KeyBackspace,
35		"delete":    tea.KeyDelete,
36		"home":      tea.KeyHome,
37		"end":       tea.KeyEnd,
38		"pgup":      tea.KeyPgUp,
39		"pgdown":    tea.KeyPgDown,
40		"ctrl+a":    tea.KeyCtrlA,
41		"ctrl+c":    tea.KeyCtrlC,
42		"ctrl+d":    tea.KeyCtrlD,
43		"ctrl+k":    tea.KeyCtrlK,
44		"ctrl+n":    tea.KeyCtrlN,
45		"ctrl+o":    tea.KeyCtrlO,
46		"ctrl+r":    tea.KeyCtrlR,
47		"ctrl+s":    tea.KeyCtrlS,
48		"ctrl+w":    tea.KeyCtrlW,
49	}
50	
51	// Key builds the tea.KeyMsg whose String() equals name.
52	//
53	// Names listed in namedKeys map to their dedicated key type ("enter", "esc",
54	// "ctrl+s", " "). Anything else is treated as literal runes, so Key("y") and
55	// Key("gg") produce the rune messages a view matching on those strings expects.
56	func Key(name string) tea.KeyMsg {
57		if kt, ok := namedKeys[name]; ok {
58			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: kt}
59		}
60		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune(name)}
61	}
62	
63	// Keys builds one message per name, for feeding a sequence to Update().
64	func Keys(names ...string) []tea.Msg {
65		msgs := make([]tea.Msg, 0, len(names))
66		for _, n := range names {
67			msgs = append(msgs, Key(n))
68		}
69		return msgs
70	}
71	
72	// Type builds one rune message per character of s, reproducing a user typing
73	// into a text input. Use this instead of Key(s) when the target is a
74	// bubbles/textinput: it consumes runes one keypress at a time.
75	func Type(s string) []tea.Msg {
76		msgs := make([]tea.Msg, 0, len(s))
77		for _, r := range s {
78			msgs = append(msgs, tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune{r}})
79		}
80		return msgs
81	}
82	
83	// Resize builds the window size message views use to lay themselves out.
84	func Resize(width, height int) tea.Msg {
85		return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: width, Height: height}
86	}
87	
88	// Msgs executes cmd and returns every message it produced, flattening the
89	// tea.Batch tree. A nil command, or one returning nil, yields no messages.
90	//
91	// The command runs synchronously on the calling goroutine. Do not pass a command
92	// that sleeps or performs I/O — tea.Tick blocks for its whole duration, and the
93	// Docker runners shell out. Assert on the command's identity or on model state
94	// instead for those.
95	func Msgs(cmd tea.Cmd) []tea.Msg {
96		if cmd == nil {
97			return nil
98		}
99		msg := cmd()
100		if msg == nil {
101			return nil
102		}
103		if batch, ok := msg.(tea.BatchMsg); ok {
104			var out []tea.Msg
105			for _, c := range batch {
106				out = append(out, Msgs(c)...)
107			}
108			return out
109		}
110		return []tea.Msg{msg}
111	}
112	
113	// Msg executes cmd and returns the single message it produced, or nil.
114	// It is the common case of Msgs for commands that emit exactly one message.
115	func Msg(cmd tea.Cmd) tea.Msg {
116		msgs := Msgs(cmd)
117		if len(msgs) == 0 {
118			return nil
119		}
120		return msgs[0]
121	}
122	
123	// MsgOf reports whether cmd produced a message of type T, returning the first
124	// such message. It searches through batched commands.
125	func MsgOf[T tea.Msg](cmd tea.Cmd) (T, bool) {
126		for _, m := range Msgs(cmd) {
127			if v, ok := m.(T); ok {
128				return v, true
129			}
130		}
131		var zero T
132		return zero, false
133	}

537	### 3.7 A command-mode key that works from inside a text field
538	
539	Requested: enter command mode with a modifier chord rather than a bare `:`,

541	but insert a colon.

543	The complaint is accurate and the current design concedes it. `internal/app/app.go:466`
544	routes `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which asks the view whether it is
545	in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it is, forwards the keystroke to
546	the active input instead. So command mode is unreachable from any form, filter
547	box or search field — which is most of the application.
548	
549	An escape hatch already exists and shows the shape of the problem: the
550	`CommandModeView` interface (`app.go:44`) lets a view declare that `:` should
551	enter command mode even while `InEditMode()` is true. Exactly one view
552	implements it — `internal/ui/netdiag/update.go:18` — and only for the topology
553	tab in its ready state, where nothing is being edited anyway. It papers over a
554	routing quirk; it does not give the user a way in while typing.
555	
556	#### Worked example: the security view
557	
558	`internal/ui/security/model.go:296` returns `InEditMode() == true` for focused
559	fields 1, 7 and 10 — target path, Trivy server, Gitleaks config. Field 7 is the
560	case that makes the point: its own placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954`,
561	so the field has to accept **two** colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:`
562	to the input there is not a bug to fix; it is the only correct behaviour.
563	
564	Which is exactly why `:` is the wrong key for command mode. The user's only
565	route out today is to move focus to a field that happens not to take text — a
566	checkbox — and press `:` there. Command-mode reachability ends up depending on
567	which control is focused, and nothing tells the user that.
568	
569	`InEditMode()` is broader still: it is also true for `StateScanning`,
570	`StateResults` and `StateDetails`, and `m.confirmModal != nil`. In those states
571	there is no field to move focus to, so `:` is forwarded to the view, which has
572	no `case` for it and drops it silently — no view in the application handles `:`
573	itself. Reaching command mode from a results table means pressing `esc` to
574	leave the results first. That is the same defect as the text field, without
575	even a workaround.
576	
577	#### `ctrl+:` specifically cannot be made to work
578	
579	Worth settling before any code is written. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing
580	bits, which only covers ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F) plus a handful of
581	aliases. `:` is 0x3A and has no control encoding: pressing Ctrl+: sends either a
582	plain `:` or nothing at all. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty
583	keyboard protocol or xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements
584	neither — the module has no reference to either. A `case "ctrl+:"` would be dead
585	code.

Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own: they are a refactor of working code with
tests already in place, and they are what makes step 5 tractable.

### 3.7 A command-mode key that works from inside a text field

Requested: enter command mode with a modifier chord rather than a bare `:`,
because the application is full of text inputs and inside one a `:` does nothing
but insert a colon.

The complaint is accurate and the current design concedes it. `internal/app/app.go:466`
routes `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which asks the view whether it is
in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it is, forwards the keystroke to
the active input instead. So command mode is unreachable from any form, filter
box or search field — which is most of the application.

An escape hatch already exists and shows the shape of the problem: the
`CommandModeView` interface (`app.go:44`) lets a view declare that `:` should
enter command mode even while `InEditMode()` is true. Exactly one view
implements it — `internal/ui/netdiag/update.go:18` — and only for the topology
tab in its ready state, where nothing is being edited anyway. It papers over a
routing quirk; it does not give the user a way in while typing.

#### Worked example: the security view

`internal/ui/security/model.go:296` returns `InEditMode() == true` for focused
fields 1, 7 and 10 — target path, Trivy server, Gitleaks config. Field 7 is the
case that makes the point: its own placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954`,
so the field has to accept **two** colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:`
to the input there is not a bug to fix; it is the only correct behaviour.

Which is exactly why `:` is the wrong key for command mode. The user's only
route out today is to move focus to a field that happens not to take text — a
checkbox — and press `:` there. Command-mode reachability ends up depending on
which control is focused, and nothing tells the user that.

`InEditMode()` is broader still: it is also true for `StateScanning`,
`StateResults` and `StateDetails`, and `m.confirmModal != nil`. In those states
there is no field to move focus to, so `:` is forwarded to the view, which has
no `case` for it and drops it silently — no view in the application handles `:`
itself. Reaching command mode from a results table means pressing `esc` to
leave the results first. That is the same defect as the text field, without
even a workaround.

#### `ctrl+:` specifically cannot be made to work

Worth settling before any code is written. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing
bits, which only covers ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F) plus a handful of
aliases. `:` is 0x3A and has no control encoding: pressing Ctrl+: sends either a
plain `:` or nothing at all. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty
keyboard protocol or xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements
neither — the module has no reference to either. A `case "ctrl+:"` would be dead
code.

#### What does work

| Option | Portability | Notes |

### 3.7 A command-mode key that works from inside a text field

Requested: enter command mode with a modifier chord rather than a bare `:`,
because the application is full of text inputs and inside one a `:` does nothing
but insert a colon.

The complaint is accurate and the current design concedes it. `internal/app/app.go:466`
routes `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which asks the view whether it is
in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it is, forwards the keystroke to
the active input instead. So command mode is unreachable from any form, filter
box or search field — which is most of the application.

An escape hatch already exists and shows the shape of the problem: the
`CommandModeView` interface (`app.go:44`) lets a view declare that `:` should
enter command mode even while `InEditMode()` is true. Exactly one view
implements it — `internal/ui/netdiag/update.go:18` — and only for the topology
tab in its ready state, where nothing is being edited anyway. It papers over a
routing quirk; it does not give the user a way in while typing.

#### Worked example: the security view

`internal/ui/security/model.go:296` returns `InEditMode() == true` for focused
fields 1, 7 and 10 — target path, Trivy server, Gitleaks config. Field 7 is the
case that makes the point: its own placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954`,
so the field has to accept **two** colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:`
to the input there is not a bug to fix; it is the only correct behaviour.

Which is exactly why `:` is the wrong key for command mode. The user's only
route out today is to move focus to a field that happens not to take text — a
checkbox — and press `:` there. Command-mode reachability ends up depending on
which control is focused, and nothing tells the user that.

`InEditMode()` is broader still: it is also true for `StateScanning`,
`StateResults` and `StateDetails`, and `m.confirmModal != nil`. In those states
there is no field to move focus to, so `:` is forwarded to the view, which has
no `case` for it and drops it silently — no view in the application handles `:`
itself. Reaching command mode from a results table means pressing `esc` to
leave the results first. That is the same defect as the text field, without
even a workaround.

#### `ctrl+:` specifically cannot be made to work

Worth settling before any code is written. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing
bits, which only covers ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F) plus a handful of
aliases. `:` is 0x3A and has no control encoding: pressing Ctrl+: sends either a
plain `:` or nothing at all. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty
keyboard protocol or xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements
neither — the module has no reference to either. A `case "ctrl+:"` would be dead
code.

| `esc` then `:` | Total | Vim-like, but `esc` already means cancel / go back everywhere (Rule 111), so it would need a mode timer. Not recommended. |

**Recommendation: keep `:` and add one chord that always wins**, rather than
replacing `:`. Muscle memory survives, and the new binding needs no
`InEditMode()` check at all — `handleKeyMsg` sees every `tea.KeyMsg` before any
view does, so a `case` there takes priority unconditionally. That is the whole
implementation: three lines next to the existing `case ":"`.

- `internal/app/app_header.go:56` renders `:` as the inactive command prompt —
  it should show whichever key is authoritative.
- `internal/app/app_test.go:30` asserts the `:` shortcut.
- Rules 114, 130 and 137: every view's `GetShortcuts()` / `GetHelpContent()` that
  mentions `:`. Three views were already caught drifting on this kind of change

### 3.7 Command mode from inside a text field — **done**

`alt+:` now opens the command line from anywhere, including a focused text
input. A bare `:` keeps its old, conditional behaviour, so muscle memory
survives.

The problem: `handleKeyMsg` routed `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which
asked the view whether it was in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it
was, forwarded the keystroke to the active input. Command mode was therefore
unreachable from any form, filter box or search field — most of the application.

The security view is the case that settles it. `InEditMode()` is true there for
the target path, Trivy server and Gitleaks config fields, and the Trivy server
placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954` — the field has to accept **two**
colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:` to the input is not a bug; it is
the only correct behaviour, which is precisely why `:` cannot be the
authoritative key. The only way in was to move focus to a control that takes no
text and press `:` there, so reachability depended on which widget was focused
and nothing said so.

It was worse in `StateScanning`, `StateResults`, `StateDetails` and while a
confirm modal is open: `InEditMode()` is true and there is no field to move
focus to. `:` was forwarded to the view, which has no `case` for it — no view in
the application handles `:` itself — and dropped silently.

#### Why `alt+`, not `ctrl+`

`ctrl+:` cannot be made to work, and this is the note that should stop anyone
reintroducing it. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing bits, which only covers
ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F). `:` is 0x3A: Ctrl+: sends a plain `:` or
nothing. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty keyboard protocol or
xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements neither. A
`case "ctrl+:"` would be dead code.

Alt has no such limit — a terminal sends ESC then the key, and bubbletea reports
that as the key carrying `Alt`. The alternative considered was a free
`ctrl+<letter>` (`b g l p t u v x z` are unused; `ctrl+i m j h [` are Tab, Enter,
LF, Backspace and Esc and must be left alone), which is marginally more portable
but loses the `:` in the gesture.

#### What shipped

- `altCommandModeKey` is handled in `handleKeyMsg` **before** the `InEditMode()`
  fork, so no view can claim it. The router sees every `tea.KeyMsg` first, which
  is what makes the binding unconditional.
- `enterCommandMode()` extracted; `maybeEnterInCommandMode` now only answers the
  bare `:`.
- `testutil.Key` understands an `alt+` prefix, building the key with the `Alt`
  modifier rather than the five literal runes `alt+:`. Both round-trip through
  `String()`, but only one is the message the application actually receives.
- Every `GetShortcuts()` and `GetHelpContent()` advertising `:` now advertises
  `alt+:` (Rules 114, 130, 137). The dashboard's Navigation help section carries
  the nuance in prose, so the other eight sites stay one line each.
- The header still renders `:` as the inactive prompt: it is the command line's
  visual marker, not a key legend, and `:` remains valid whenever no field has
  focus.

Two things the ripple list got wrong, corrected here: `app_test.go:30` is a
layout fixture for `buildShortcutLines`, not an assertion about the binding, so
it was left alone. And `CommandModeView` / `AllowCommandMode` was not merely
made redundant by this change — **it was already dead code**. The router only
consulted it when `InEditMode()` was true, and netdiag's implementation returns
true only on the topology tab, where `InEditMode()` is unconditionally false. It
could never fire. Deleted, along with its one implementation;
`TestCommandModeOnTheTopologyTab` became
`TestTheTopologyTabNeverBlocksCommandMode` and records why.

gh pr edit 16 --title "feat: open command mode with alt+: from anywhere, including a text field" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`alt+:` now opens the command line from anywhere, including a focused text input. A bare `:` keeps its old, conditional behaviour, so muscle memory survives. Records the whole thing in `docs/backlog.md` §3.7.

## The problem

`handleKeyMsg` routed `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which forwards the keystroke to the active input whenever `FormView.InEditMode()` is true. Command mode was unreachable from any form, filter box or search field.

The security view settles it: `InEditMode()` is true for the target path, Trivy server and Gitleaks config fields, and the Trivy server placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954` — the field has to accept **two** colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:` there is correct, not a bug, which is exactly why `:` cannot be the authoritative key. The only way in was to move focus to a control that takes no text and press `:` there.

Worse in `StateScanning` / `StateResults` / `StateDetails` and with a confirm modal open: `InEditMode()` is true and there is no field to move to. `:` was forwarded to the view, which has no `case` for it, and dropped silently.

## Why `alt+`, not `ctrl+`

`ctrl+:` cannot work. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing bits, covering only ASCII `@`–`_` (0x40–0x5F); `:` is 0x3A, so Ctrl+: sends a plain `:` or nothing. Reporting it needs the Kitty keyboard protocol or xterm `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements neither. Alt has no such limit — the terminal sends ESC then the key, and bubbletea reports it as the key carrying `Alt`.

## Changes

- `altCommandModeKey` handled in `handleKeyMsg` **before** the `InEditMode()` fork, so no view can claim it.
- `enterCommandMode()` extracted; `maybeEnterInCommandMode` now only answers the bare `:`.
- `testutil.Key` understands an `alt+` prefix, building the key with the `Alt` modifier rather than the five literal runes `alt+:`. Both round-trip through `String()`; only one is the message the application receives.
- Every `GetShortcuts()` / `GetHelpContent()` advertising `:` now advertises `alt+:` (Rules 114, 130, 137). The dashboard's Navigation section carries the nuance in prose so the other eight sites stay one line each.
- Header keeps `:` as the inactive prompt — it marks the command line rather than being a key legend, and `:` is still valid with nothing focused.

## Dead code found

`CommandModeView` / `AllowCommandMode` was not merely made redundant by this change — **it could never fire**. The router consulted it only when `InEditMode()` was true, and netdiag's sole implementation covers the topology tab, where `InEditMode()` is unconditionally false. Deleted; `TestCommandModeOnTheTopologyTab` became `TestTheTopologyTabNeverBlocksCommandMode` and records why.

Also corrected: `app_test.go:30` turned out to be a layout fixture for `buildShortcutLines`, not an assertion about the binding, so it was left alone.

## Test plan

- [x] `internal/app/command_mode_test.go` — first tests in the package: `alt+:` opens the command line while the view is editing and is not forwarded to it; a bare `:` opens it with nothing focused and reaches the field otherwise; entering asks for a resize and clears the input.
- [x] `testutil` — `alt+` prefix over runes and named keys, plus the bare `alt+` literal case. Package stays at 100 %.
- [x] `mise run lint` → 0 issues.
- [x] `go test ./...` → all packages pass.
- [ ] `mise run test-race` — CI (no local C compiler).
EOF
)" && gh pr checks 16 --watch 2>&1 | tail -5

`alt+:` est implémenté — #16 est passé de « entrée backlog » à la feature complète, CI verte (lint 0 issue, tests + race detector).

**Le cœur du changement** tient en une ligne bien placée : `altCommandModeKey` est traité dans `handleKeyMsg` **avant** le fork `InEditMode()`. Le routeur voit tous les `tea.KeyMsg` avant n'importe quelle vue, donc aucun champ texte ne peut le réclamer. `:` garde son comportement conditionnel — la mémoire musculaire survit.

**Deux surprises en cours de route :**

`CommandModeView` / `AllowCommandMode` n'est pas devenu redondant avec ce changement — **c'était déjà du code mort**. Le routeur ne le consultait que quand `InEditMode()` était vrai, et l'unique implémentation (netdiag) ne couvre que l'onglet topology, où `InEditMode()` renvoie `false` inconditionnellement. Il ne pouvait jamais se déclencher. Supprimé ; `TestCommandModeOnTheTopologyTab` devient `TestTheTopologyTabNeverBlocksCommandMode` et documente pourquoi.

Et `app_test.go:30`, que j'avais listé dans le ripple comme « assertion sur le raccourci `:` », est en fait une fixture de layout pour `buildShortcutLines` — la liste de raccourcis y est arbitraire. Laissée telle quelle.

**Un détail de test qui compte :** `testutil.Key("alt+:")` construisait naïvement les cinq runes `a l t + :`, dont le `String()` vaut aussi `"alt+:"`. Le test serait passé sans rien prouver. `Key` comprend maintenant le préfixe `alt+` et pose le modificateur `Alt` sur la touche qui suit — c'est-à-dire exactement le message que bubbletea délivre quand le terminal envoie ESC puis `:`. `testutil` reste à 100 %.

Côté aide, les neuf sites qui annonçaient `:` annoncent `alt+:` (Rules 114/130/137). La nuance — « `:` marche aussi, mais seulement hors champ texte » — est écrite une seule fois, dans la section Navigation de l'aide du dashboard, avec l'exemple `https://trivy-server:4954`. Le header garde `:` comme prompt inactif : c'est le marqueur visuel de la ligne de commande, pas une légende de touche.

Reste : merger #16, puis reprendre la phase 3 sur `explorer` (1402 lignes).

361		if tableDataHeight < 1 {
362			tableDataHeight = 1
363		}
364		m.table.SetHeight(tableDataHeight)
365	
366		// Column widths (Rule 116: contentWidth = width - 2, available = contentWidth - numColumns*2)
367		contentWidth := width - 2
368		available := contentWidth - numColumns*2
369	
370		columns := m.table.Columns()
371		if len(columns) >= numColumns {
372			columns[0].Width = int(float64(available) * colTypeRatio)
373			columns[1].Width = int(float64(available) * colNameRatio)
374			columns[2].Width = int(float64(available) * colSlugRatio)
375			columns[3].Width = int(float64(available) * colVisibilityRatio)
376			columns[4].Width = int(float64(available) * colRoleRatio)
377			columns[5].Width = int(float64(available) * colCreatedRatio)
378			columns[6].Width = int(float64(available) * colActivityRatio)
379			// Last column gets the remainder
380			columns[7].Width = available - columns[0].Width - columns[1].Width - columns[2].Width - columns[3].Width - columns[4].Width - columns[5].Width - columns[6].Width
381			m.table.SetColumns(columns)
382		}
383	}
384	
385	// updateTableRows rebuilds table rows from current items (sorted), applying active filters
386	func (m *Model) updateTableRows() {
387		query := strings.ToLower(m.filterBar.SearchQuery())
388		items := m.sortedItems(m.currentItems())
389		rows := make([]table.Row, 0, len(items))
390		for _, node := range items {
391			if query != "" {
392				nameMatch := strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(node.Name), query)
393				pathMatch := strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(node.FullPath), query)
394				if !nameMatch && !pathMatch {
395					continue
396				}
397			}
398			rows = append(rows, table.Row{
399				nodeTypeLabel(node),
400				node.Name,
401				nodeSlug(node.FullPath),
402				visibilityLabel(node),
403				node.AccessLevelName(),
404				timeAgo(node.CreatedAt),
405				timeAgo(node.LastActivityAt),
406				pipelineStatusLabel(node),
407			})
408		}
409		m.table.SetRows(rows)
410		m.updateSortIndicators()
411	}
412	
413	// cycleSort cycles through sort options: each column asc then desc, then next column
414	func (m Model) cycleSort() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
415		if m.sortAsc {
416			m.sortAsc = false
417		} else {
418			m.sortAsc = true
419			nextIdx := 0
420			for i, col := range sortableColumns {
421				if col == m.sortColumn {
422					nextIdx = (i + 1) % len(sortableColumns)
423					break
424				}
425			}
426			m.sortColumn = sortableColumns[nextIdx]
427		}
428		m.updateTableRows()
429		return m, nil
430	}
431	
432	// sortedItems returns nodes sorted by the current sort column and direction
433	func (m *Model) sortedItems(items []*TreeNode) []*TreeNode {
434		if len(items) == 0 {
435			return items
436		}
437	
438		sorted := make([]*TreeNode, len(items))
439		copy(sorted, items)
440	
441		sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
442			a, b := sorted[i], sorted[j]
443	
444			var less bool
445			switch m.sortColumn {
446			case sortByName:
447				less = strings.ToLower(a.Name) < strings.ToLower(b.Name)
448			case sortByVisibility:
449				less = strings.ToLower(a.Visibility) < strings.ToLower(b.Visibility)
450			case sortByCreated:
451				less = timeBefore(a.CreatedAt, b.CreatedAt)
452			case sortByActivity:
453				less = timeBefore(a.LastActivityAt, b.LastActivityAt)
454			default: // sortByType
455				less = string(a.Type) < string(b.Type)
456			}
457	
458			if m.sortAsc {
459				return less
460			}
461			return !less
462		})
463	
464		return sorted
465	}
466	
467	// timeBefore compares two nullable times (nil is considered "oldest")
468	func timeBefore(a, b *time.Time) bool {
469		if a == nil && b == nil {
470			return false
471		}
472		if a == nil {
473			return true
474		}
475		if b == nil {
476			return false
477		}
478		return a.Before(*b)
479	}
480	
481	// updateSortIndicators updates column headers with ▲/▼ sort arrows
482	func (m *Model) updateSortIndicators() {
483		sortColIndex := map[sortField]int{
484			sortByType:       0,
485			sortByName:       1,
486			sortByVisibility: 3,
487			sortByCreated:    5,
488			sortByActivity:   6,
489		}
490		baseTitles := map[int]string{
491			0: "Type",
492			1: "Name",
493			3: "Visibility",
494			5: "Created",
495			6: "Activity",
496		}
497	
498		columns := m.table.Columns()
499		if len(columns) < numColumns {
500			return
501		}
502	
503		// Reset sortable column titles
504		for idx, title := range baseTitles {
505			columns[idx].Title = title
506		}
507	
508		// Add arrow to active sort column
509		if idx, ok := sortColIndex[m.sortColumn]; ok {
510			arrow := " ▲"
511			if !m.sortAsc {
512				arrow = " ▼"
513			}
514			columns[idx].Title = baseTitles[idx] + arrow
515		}
516	
517		m.table.SetColumns(columns)
518	}
519	
520	// handleDrillDown handles enter key - navigate into a group
521	func (m Model) handleDrillDown(items []*TreeNode) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
522		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
523		if cursor >= len(items) {
524			return m, nil
525		}
526		node := items[cursor]
527		if node.Type != NodeTypeGroup {
528			return m, nil
529		}

test: cover the gitlab explorer and fix three defects it exposed

Three defects the tests exposed, each pinned by a test that failed first:

- Actions resolved the cursor against the unfiltered list while the table
  showed the filtered one. With a filter active, ctrl+d, p, → and ctrl+w all
  acted on a different resource than the highlighted row — deleting the wrong
  group is the worst case. handleKeyMsg and GetShortcuts now go through
  visibleItems(), the same list updateTableRows builds from.

- bubbles does not clamp the table cursor when the row count shrinks, so
  narrowing the filter left it past the end: nothing highlighted and every
  action silently doing nothing. Same defect fixed in workspaces (#15); the
  drill-down path was already safe because it calls GotoTop().

  left the message on screen permanently (Rule 128).
EOF

**A stranded cursor in the workspaces table.** `bubbles/table.SetRows` does not
clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks. Drilling into a directory with
fewer entries — or narrowing the filter — left the cursor past the end: nothing
highlighted, and `enter`, `ctrl+d`, `r` and `ctrl+s` all silently did nothing

input.new_string:
**The explorer acted on a different row than the one highlighted.** Found in
phase 3, and the most serious defect the coverage work has turned up.

`handleKeyMsg` resolved the cursor against `sortedItems(currentItems())` — the
unfiltered list — while the table was built from the filtered one. With a filter
active the two indices disagree, so `ctrl+d`, `p`, `→` and `ctrl+w` all acted on
whatever happened to sit at that index in the *unfiltered* list. Filtering to a
single project and pressing `ctrl+d` scheduled a different group for deletion.
`GetShortcuts` had it too, so even the advertised `ctrl+w` keyed off the wrong
node.

Both now go through `visibleItems()`, the single list `updateTableRows` builds
from. Pinned by `TestActionsResolveTheRowTheUserCanSee`, which filters to a row
that sits at a different index in each list — the fixtures were chosen so the
two cannot coincide.

**A stranded cursor in the workspaces table.** `bubbles/table.SetRows` does not
clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks. Drilling into a directory with
fewer entries — or narrowing the filter — left the cursor past the end: nothing
highlighted, and `enter`, `ctrl+d`, `r` and `ctrl+s` all silently did nothing
until the user pressed an arrow key. `updateTableData` now clamps.

The containers view avoids this by calling `GotoTop()` after every filter
change; workspaces had no equivalent. **`explorer` had it too**, and only on the
filter path — its drill-down was already safe because it calls `GotoTop()`.
Fixed the same way.

**A footer message with no timer.** `explorer.handleDeleteComplete` set
`footerError` and returned `nil`, so a failed delete left "Delete failed — check
logs" on screen until something else overwrote it. Rule 128 caps footer messages
at three seconds, and the same file's `BrowserOpenedMsg` handler already did it
correctly. Now returns `clearFooterErrorCmd()`.

Phase 3, in progress:

| Package | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/ui/netdiag` | 15.9 % | **86.1 %** |
| `internal/ui/workspaces` | 0 % | **81.3 %** |
| `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer` | 0 % | **91.5 %** |

The three-step order held on all three: surface pass 58.8 % / 60.3 % / 58.1 %,
split with the figure unchanged to the statement, completion pass to 86.1 % /
81.3 % / 91.5 %.

`workspaces` added one technique worth reusing: its filesystem commands
(`createWorkspace`, `deleteEntry`, `renameEntry`, `loadEntries`, `enrichEntry`)
are **executed** rather than asserted on identity, against `t.TempDir()` and a
throwaway git repository. That is what proves the branch, remote and dirty-tree
counters are read correctly; a stub would only prove the stub works. It skips
when `git` is not on `PATH`, like `internal/gitlab` does. Only the Docker- and
desktop-backed commands are left alone.

`explorer` extended that to the API layer, which is why it reaches 91.5 % —
higher than either of the others despite having the largest untestable-looking
surface. The rule that emerged: **execute the command whenever the dependency
can be stood up locally**, and only fall back to asserting on model state when
it cannot.

| Dependency | Treatment |
|---|---|
| GitLab API | executed against `httptest` — the SDK takes a base URL |
| OCI registry | executed against `httptest` |
| git | executed against a seeded repository, skipped without `git` on `PATH` |
| Desktop browser | not executed; the guard branches are driven, the launch is not |

The pull tests are the clearest case: the "GitLab host" is a local directory
holding seeded repositories, so `recursivePull` really clones and really writes
the directory tree. That is what proves the tree mirrors the group hierarchy,
that an existing checkout is skipped rather than clobbered, and that a group
whose children were never browsed is fetched mid-pull. `cloneURL` was extracted
from `pullProject` to make the SSH and HTTPS URL shapes assertable — `gitlab.Clone`
reports only an exit status, so the URL it was handed is not observable through
the error.

The rest of phase 3 is `security` (1977 lines).

Existing users must re-authenticate: credentials saved under the old
path-stripped key no longer match. Those credentials were ambiguous across
contexts anyway.

Two smaller defects went with it:

- `Delete` had no timeout, while `Save` and `Load` bounded themselves to 2 s
  precisely so an unconfigured helper could not freeze the TUI. Logout could
  hang indefinitely.
- The timeout killed only the direct `git` child, though its comment claimed
  otherwise. The helper git spawns survives and holds the output pipes open, so
  `Run` kept blocking. All three calls now share one `runCredential` helper built
  on `exec.CommandContext` plus `WaitDelay`, which bounds the wait on those pipes.

`internal/credentials/helper.go` (`HelperStorage`, 137 lines) was deleted rather
than fixed: nothing outside its own tests constructed it. It was also broken —
`detectHelper()` returns whatever `git config credential.helper` holds, so a
common value like `store --file=/path` became the single unfindable command

1	# DevDesk Backlog
2	
3	**Last Updated:** 2026-08-02
4	
5	Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
6	Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
7	(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
8	rather than carried over.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Known defects
13	
14	D1, D3 and D6 (the byte-vs-rune lot), then D2, D5 and D7, were fixed; see
15	[§1.1](#11-fixed). **D4 is the only one left**, and it is waiting on a decision
16	rather than on work.
17	
18	### D4 — `DeleteConfirmModal` uses `Tab` for field navigation
19	
20	`internal/ui/components/delete_confirm_modal.go:89-97`
21	
22	`tab` / `shift+tab` cycle checkbox → Yes → No. Rule 135 reserves those keys for
23	tab switching and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively.
24	
25	Cosmetic in isolation, but it is the kind of inconsistency Rule 135 exists to
26	prevent. Changing it alters muscle memory, so it needs a deliberate call rather
27	than a drive-by fix.
28	
29	Note that the surrounding code moved when D2 was fixed: `tab` / `shift+tab` now
30	cycle through `cycleFocus()`, which skips the locked checkbox. Switching to
31	`↑ / ↓` remains a one-line change to the key names.
32	
33	### D8 — Write-only CRUD flags and an unreachable handler in the status view
34	
35	`internal/ui/status/model.go:64-67` and `internal/ui/status/update.go:57-60`
36	
37	`Model.creating`, `Model.editing` and `Model.confirming` are assigned in five
38	places and read in none: the view keys off `componentForm != nil` and
39	`confirmModal != nil` instead. `HasActiveForm`, the one method that read them, is
40	commented out at `model.go:139`.
41	
42	`ComponentFormCancelledMsg` is never sent either. `ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg`
43	answers `esc` by returning a nil form, and the caller stores that — so the
44	`case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg` branch in `Update()` cannot run. Its
45	body is the only thing that would reset `creating` / `editing`, which is why they
46	would stay true after a cancellation if anything did read them.
47	
48	Harmless today, but it is state that lies: a reader reasonably assumes those
49	flags mean something. Found while writing the phase 2 tests; the tests
50	deliberately assert on `componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags,
51	so removing them breaks nothing.
52	
53	**Fix:** delete the three fields, the unreachable case and the message type — or
54	give `esc` a message and make the flags load-bearing. Deleting is the smaller
55	change and matches how the view already works.
56	
57	### D9 — The containers list opens sorted Z→A
58	
59	`internal/ui/containers/model.go:140-147`
60	
61	`New()` sets neither `sortColumn` nor `sortAsc`, so both take their zero value:
62	name, *descending*. The status view, which has the same cycle-sort mechanism,
63	sets `sortAsc: true` explicitly. The header does show `Name ▼`, so the view is
64	at least honest about it — but nobody chose it, and it disagrees with the other
65	list view in the application.
66	
67	**Fix:** set `sortAsc: true` in `New()`, one line. Left for a deliberate call
68	because it changes what the user sees on open.
69	`TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending` pins the current behaviour and says so.
70	
71	### 1.1 Fixed
72	
73	**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
74	phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.
75	
76	The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while
77	the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
78	was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.
79	The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`
80	without documenting it at all.
81	
82	The workspaces view had it too, found in phase 3: `n` and `Enter` documented
83	where the bindings are `ctrl+n` and `enter`, `/` undocumented, and the same
84	stale "Press [n]" in its empty state.
85	
86	`explorer` made it four in a row, though only just: every key was documented
87	except `/`. The check caught it on its first run.
88	
89	All four are fixed, and each package now asserts that every key
90	`GetShortcuts()` advertises appears in `GetHelpContent()` — the check that would
91	have caught the drift when it was introduced. Assume `security` has it too.
92	
93	**The explorer acted on a different row than the one highlighted.** Found in
94	phase 3, and the most serious defect the coverage work has turned up.
95	
96	`handleKeyMsg` resolved the cursor against `sortedItems(currentItems())` — the
97	unfiltered list — while the table was built from the filtered one. With a filter
98	active the two indices disagree, so `ctrl+d`, `p`, `→` and `ctrl+w` all acted on
99	whatever happened to sit at that index in the *unfiltered* list. Filtering to a
100	single project and pressing `ctrl+d` scheduled a different group for deletion.
101	`GetShortcuts` had it too, so even the advertised `ctrl+w` keyed off the wrong
102	node.
103	
104	Both now go through `visibleItems()`, the single list `updateTableRows` builds
105	from. Pinned by `TestActionsResolveTheRowTheUserCanSee`, which filters to a row
106	that sits at a different index in each list — the fixtures were chosen so the
107	two cannot coincide.
108	
109	**A stranded cursor in the workspaces table.** `bubbles/table.SetRows` does not
110	clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks. Drilling into a directory with
111	fewer entries — or narrowing the filter — left the cursor past the end: nothing
112	highlighted, and `enter`, `ctrl+d`, `r` and `ctrl+s` all silently did nothing
113	until the user pressed an arrow key. `updateTableData` now clamps.
114	
115	The containers view avoids this by calling `GotoTop()` after every filter
116	change; workspaces had no equivalent. **`explorer` had it too**, and only on the
117	filter path — its drill-down was already safe because it calls `GotoTop()`.
118	Fixed the same way.
119	
120	**A footer message with no timer.** `explorer.handleDeleteComplete` set
121	`footerError` and returned `nil`, so a failed delete left "Delete failed — check
122	logs" on screen until something else overwrote it. Rule 128 caps footer messages
123	at three seconds, and the same file's `BrowserOpenedMsg` handler already did it
124	correctly. Now returns `clearFooterErrorCmd()`.
125	
126	**D7** (`extractTarGz` kept parent references in archive paths), **D2** (the
127	"permanent delete" checkbox was documented as locked but was not) and **D5** (an
128	unreachable focus clamp in `CreationForm`) were fixed together — three small,
129	independent defects with no shared code.
130	
131	`extractTarGz` now routes every member name through `sanitizeArchivePath`, which
132	normalises the separators and rejects anything resolving outside the root.
133	Cleaning happens *after* the leading separator is stripped, not before:
134	`path.Clean("/../x")` returns `"/x"`, which would have absorbed the traversal
135	silently instead of exposing it. Traversal that resolves back inside the root
136	(`templates/../README.md`) is kept, normalised. Backslashes are folded to `/`
137	first, so `..\..\etc\passwd` cannot pass as an ordinary filename on a tar reader
138	that treats it as one.

142	navigation skips the checkbox entirely (`minFocus()` / `cycleFocus()`) and the
143	line renders dimmed: a focusable control that ignores every key is more

145

154	`TestExtractTarGzRejectsParentTraversal` (table-driven over five escape shapes)

The project's own coding rules cap files at 800 lines. Five still exceed it:

`update.go`, `run.go`, `view.go` and `header.go`; the largest is now 314 lines
and `model.go` itself is 172. `topology_model.go` stays at 752 — under the
ceiling, and its parsers and renderer belong together.

`internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` (1299 lines) was split into `messages.go`,
`table.go`, `entry.go`, `actions.go` and `update.go`; the largest is 450 and
`model.go` itself is 129. `entry.go` is the one worth noticing: the pure and
filesystem-only helpers now sit together instead of at the bottom of a
1300-line model, which is what made them straightforward to cover.

`internal/docker/client.go` (1176 lines — the 1069 recorded earlier was stale)
was split into `exec.go`, `containers.go`, `images.go`, `networks.go`,
`volumes.go`, `registry.go`, `launch.go`, `system.go` and `parse.go`; the largest
is now 269 lines. The former `network.go` became `ports.go`, since it reports the
host's listening sockets via `ss` rather than Docker networks — the name was
free for the `docker network` family.

This interacts with the coverage work: writing several thousand statements of
tests against these files before splitting them freezes their current structure.
Decide the order deliberately. Splitting `docker` first was the cheap case — its
7.3 % coverage meant almost no tests were pinned to the old shape.

the surface pass reached 58.8 % driving `Update()` and `View()` only, the split
moved five blocks of code with the coverage figure unchanged to the statement,
and the completion pass took it to 86.1 %. The discipline that makes it work is
asserting on behaviour rather than on internals — no test named a file, and the
only ones that reach into the model do so for state the view has no other way to

`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:445-449` and `:493-496`

When the OCI registry cannot be reached, the explorer opens the creation form
anyway and calls `SetTemplateWarning("Registry error: …")` — the right call.

warning sits below that return and never renders. The user sees a Template
field offering nothing but "none", with no indication that the list failed to
load rather than being genuinely empty.

Reaching it takes four keystrokes: switch the type to Project, then move focus
down to Template. Nothing suggests doing so.

Found in phase 3 while covering the explorer.

*not* visible on the unfocused field, and that it appears once focused — so the
test fails in both directions when this is fixed, and says so.

**Fix:** render the warning outside the focused/unfocused branch, or surface it
on the form as a whole rather than on the field. Left for a deliberate call
because it changes a shared component used by more than the explorer.

| | Coverage | `model.go` |
|---|---|---|
| before | 0 % | 1402 lines |

The split moved code with the coverage figure unchanged to the statement, as on `netdiag` and `workspaces`. Three packages in, that is now the default rather than an experiment.

## Three defects fixed, each pinned by a test that failed first

**Actions acted on a different row than the one highlighted.** `handleKeyMsg` resolved the cursor against the *unfiltered* list while the table was built from the filtered one. With a filter active, `ctrl+d`, `p`, `→` and `ctrl+w` all acted on whatever sat at that index in the unfiltered list — filtering to a single project and pressing `ctrl+d` scheduled a different group for deletion. `GetShortcuts` had it too. Both now go through `visibleItems()`. The fixtures in `TestActionsResolveTheRowTheUserCanSee` are chosen so the two indices cannot coincide.

**A stranded cursor**, the same one fixed in workspaces (#15): `bubbles/table.SetRows` does not clamp when the row count shrinks. Here it only affected the filter path — drill-down was already safe because it calls `GotoTop()`.

**A footer message with no timer.** `handleDeleteComplete` set `footerError` and returned `nil`, so a failed delete stayed on screen indefinitely (Rule 128). The same file's browser handler already did it correctly.

## Help drift, fourth view in a row

`/` was advertised in `GetShortcuts()` and absent from `GetHelpContent()`. The check added in status, containers and workspaces caught it on its first run here. Only `security` left to check.

## One new open defect: D10

A registry failure sets a warning on the creation form that `renderTemplateList` never reaches — it returns early when the field is unfocused, and the warning sits below that return. The user sees a Template field offering only "none", with nothing to say the list failed to load. Reaching the warning takes four keystrokes. Recorded rather than fixed: it touches a shared component. `TestTemplateFailureStillOpensTheForm` pins both halves, so it fails in both directions when someone fixes it.

## The testing rule this package settled

Execute the command whenever the dependency can be stood up locally; fall back to asserting on model state only when it cannot.

| Dependency | Treatment |
|---|---|
| GitLab API | executed against `httptest` — the SDK takes a base URL |
| OCI registry | executed against `httptest` |
| git | executed against a seeded repository, skipped without `git` on `PATH` |
| Desktop browser | not executed; the guard branches are driven, the launch is not |

The pull tests are the clearest case: the "GitLab host" is a local directory of seeded repositories, so `recursivePull` really clones and really writes the tree. That is what proves the directory layout mirrors the group hierarchy, that an existing checkout is skipped rather than clobbered, and that a group whose children were never browsed is fetched mid-pull.

`cloneURL` was extracted from `pullProject` so the SSH and HTTPS shapes can be asserted directly — `gitlab.Clone` reports only an exit status, so the URL it was handed is not observable through the error.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run lint` → 0 issues.
- [x] `go test ./...` → all packages pass.
- [x] Split verified as a pure move: the only non-import difference is a dropped `// Messages` section header.
- [ ] `mise run test-race` — CI (no local C compiler).
EOF

Troisième paquet de la phase 3 fait : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/17 — CI verte (lint 0 issue, tests + race detector).

| | Couverture | `model.go` |
|---|---|---|
| avant | 0 % | 1402 lignes |
| étape 1 (surface) | **58,1 %** | 1402 |
| étape 2 (découpe) | **58,1 %** | **206** |
| étape 3 (complément) | **91,5 %** | 206 |
| global | 43,6 % → **49,3 %** | |

Trois paquets, trois fois la même chose : la découpe ne bouge pas la couverture d'un statement. Ce n'est plus une expérience, c'est le défaut.

**La trouvaille la plus sérieuse depuis le début de ce travail.** `handleKeyMsg` résolvait le curseur sur la liste **non filtrée** alors que le tableau était construit sur la filtrée. Avec un filtre actif les deux index divergent : `ctrl+d`, `p`, `→` et `ctrl+w` agissaient sur ce qui se trouvait à cet index dans l'autre liste. Concrètement, tu filtres sur un projet, tu presses `ctrl+d` sur la seule ligne visible, et c'est un **autre groupe** qui part en suppression. `GetShortcuts` avait le même bug, donc même le `ctrl+w` annoncé se basait sur le mauvais nœud. Les deux passent maintenant par `visibleItems()`, et les fixtures du test sont choisies pour que les deux index ne puissent pas coïncider par accident.

Deux autres corrigées au passage : le curseur bloqué (identique à workspaces, ici seulement sur le chemin filtre — le drill-down était déjà sauvé par son `GotoTop()`), et un message de footer sans timer sur l'échec de suppression (Rule 128) alors que le handler du navigateur, dans le même fichier, le faisait correctement.

**Dérive de l'aide, quatrième vue d'affilée** — `/` annoncé, absent de l'aide. Le check attrapé au premier run. Reste `security` à vérifier.

**Une nouvelle entrée D10** : quand le registre OCI est injoignable, `SetTemplateWarning` est bien appelé, mais `renderTemplateList` retourne tôt quand le champ n'a pas le focus, et l'avertissement est écrit après ce return. L'utilisateur voit une liste de templates vide sans rien qui distingue « le registre a échoué » de « il n'y a pas de template ». Il faut quatre frappes pour l'atteindre. Laissée ouverte : c'est un composant partagé. Le test épingle les deux sens, il échouera aussi quand quelqu'un corrigera.

**La règle que ce paquet a fixée**, et qui explique qu'il monte plus haut que les deux autres malgré une surface I/O bien plus grande : **exécuter la commande dès que la dépendance peut être montée localement**. `httptest` pour l'API GitLab et le registre OCI, un vrai dépôt git semé pour le clone — l'« hôte GitLab » est un répertoire local, donc `recursivePull` clone réellement et écrit réellement l'arborescence. C'est ce qui prouve que la structure de dossiers reflète la hiérarchie de groupes, qu'un checkout existant est ignoré et non écrasé, et qu'un groupe jamais parcouru est chargé en cours de pull. Seul le navigateur reste non exécuté.

Un incident à noter : le premier run CI a échoué là où le local passait. Mon faux serveur routait en itérant une map, et `/api/v4/groups/1/members/all/1` matche deux préfixes — Go randomise l'ordre, donc une fois sur deux le lookup de membre décodait une liste de groupes. Préfixes triés du plus long au plus court, vérifié avec `-count=20`.

Reste en phase 3 : `security` (1977 lignes), le dernier.

349		case tea.KeyMsg:
350			// Pass key messages to confirm modal if active
351			if m.confirmModal != nil {
352				var cmd tea.Cmd
353				m.confirmModal, cmd = m.confirmModal.Update(msg)
354				return m, cmd
355			}
356			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
357	
358		case DepsCheckedMsg:
359			m.deps = msg.Deps
360			return m, nil
361	
362		case ScanCompleteMsg:
363			return m.handleScanComplete(msg)
364	
365		case SecretIgnoredMsg:
366			if msg.Error != nil {
367				log.Printf("ERROR [security] ignore secret %s: %v", msg.Finding.File, msg.Error)
368				m.statusMessage = "Failed to ignore secret — check logs"
369			} else {
370				m.statusMessage = fmt.Sprintf("Added %s to .gitleaksignore", msg.Finding.File)
371			}
372			return m, nil
373	
374		case SelectionResultMsg:
375			m.targetPath = msg.Path
376			m.targetInput.SetValue(msg.Path)
377			return m, nil
378	
379		case SelectionCancelledMsg:
380			return m, nil
381	
382		case StartScanMsg:
383			return m.startScan()
384	
385		case ScanProgressMsg:
386			return m.handleScanProgress(msg)
387	
388		case spinner.TickMsg:
389			if m.state == StateScanning {
390				var cmd tea.Cmd
391				m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
392				return m, cmd
393			}
394		}
395	
396		return m, nil
397	}

399	// handleKeyMsg processes keyboard input
400	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
401		switch m.state {
402		case StateInput:
403			return m.handleInputState(msg)
404		case StateScanning:
405			if msg.String() == "esc" || msg.String() == "ctrl+c" {
406				return m.cancelCurrentScan()
407			}
408			return m, nil
409		case StateResults:
410			return m.handleResultsState(msg)
411		case StateDetails:
412			return m.handleDetailsState(msg)
413		}
414		return m, nil
415	}
416	
417	// totalFields returns the number of form fields
418	func (m Model) totalFields() int {
419		return 13 // 0-6 (left) + 7-11 (right, with ignoreEOL at 9) + 12 (start button)
420	}
421	
422	// isServerMode returns true when a Trivy server URL is configured.
423	func (m Model) isServerMode() bool {
424		return strings.TrimSpace(m.trivyServerInput.Value()) != ""
425	}

427	// isServerIncompatibleField returns true for scan options that are not supported
428	// by the Trivy client-server protocol (misconfig=4, license=5, sbom=6).
429	func (m Model) isServerIncompatibleField(fieldIdx int) bool {
430		return fieldIdx == 4 || fieldIdx == 5 || fieldIdx == 6
431	}
432	
433	// isFieldSkipped returns true when a field should be bypassed during Tab navigation.
434	func (m Model) isFieldSkipped(fieldIdx int) bool {
435		return m.isServerMode() && m.isServerIncompatibleField(fieldIdx)
436	}
437	
438	// nextField returns the next focusable field index, skipping disabled fields.
439	func (m Model) nextField() int {
440		total := m.totalFields()
441		next := (m.focusedField + 1) % total
442		for m.isFieldSkipped(next) {
443			next = (next + 1) % total
444		}
445		return next
446	}
447	
448	// prevField returns the previous focusable field index, skipping disabled fields.
449	func (m Model) prevField() int {
450		total := m.totalFields()
451		prev := (m.focusedField - 1 + total) % total
452		for m.isFieldSkipped(prev) {
453			prev = (prev - 1 + total) % total
454		}
455		return prev
456	}

458	// applyServerModeConstraints auto-disables options incompatible with Trivy server mode
459	// and persists the updated config. No-op when not in server mode.
460	func (m *Model) applyServerModeConstraints() {
461		if !m.isServerMode() {
462			return
463		}
464		m.enableMisconfig = false
465		m.enableLicense = false
466		m.generateSBOM = false
467		m.saveOptionsToConfig()
468	}

471	func (m Model) isTextInputField(idx int) bool {

473	}

476	func (m *Model) blurAllTextInputs() {
477		m.targetInput.Blur()
478		m.trivyServerInput.Blur()
479		m.gitleaksConfigInput.Blur()
480	}

482	// saveOptionsToConfig syncs all form options to config and persists to disk.
483	func (m Model) saveOptionsToConfig() {
484		m.config.Scan.EnableVuln = m.enableVuln
485		m.config.Scan.EnableSecret = m.enableSecret
486		m.config.Scan.EnableMisconfig = m.enableMisconfig
487		m.config.Scan.EnableLicense = m.enableLicense
488		m.config.Scan.GenerateSBOM = m.generateSBOM
489		m.config.Scan.IgnoreUnfixed = m.ignoreUnfixed
490		m.config.Scan.IgnoreEOL = m.ignoreEOL

497	// focusTextField focuses the text input for the given field index
498	func (m *Model) focusTextField(idx int) {
499		switch idx {
500		case 1:
501			m.targetInput.Focus()
502		case 7:
503			m.trivyServerInput.Focus()
504		case 10:
505			m.gitleaksConfigInput.Focus()
506		}
507	}

509	// handleInputState processes input in form state
510	func (m Model) handleInputState(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
511		// Handle text input fields (1=target, 7=trivy server, 10=gitleaks config)
512		if m.isTextInputField(m.focusedField) {
513			switch msg.String() {
514			case "down":
515				switch m.focusedField {
516				case 7:
517					m.applyServerModeConstraints()
518				case 10:
519					m.saveOptionsToConfig()
520				}
521				m.blurAllTextInputs()
522				m.focusedField = m.nextField()
523				if m.isTextInputField(m.focusedField) {
524					m.focusTextField(m.focusedField)
525				}
526				return m, nil
527			case "up":
528				switch m.focusedField {
529				case 7:
530					m.applyServerModeConstraints()
531				case 10:
532					m.saveOptionsToConfig()
533				}
534				m.blurAllTextInputs()
535				m.focusedField = m.prevField()
536				if m.isTextInputField(m.focusedField) {
537					m.focusTextField(m.focusedField)
538				}
539				return m, nil
540			case "b":
541				if m.focusedField == 1 {
542					if m.targetType == "directory" {
543						return m.openFileBrowser()
544					}
545					if m.targetType == "image" {
546						return m.openImageBrowser()
547					}
548				}
549				fallthrough
550			default:
551				var cmd tea.Cmd
552				switch m.focusedField {
553				case 1:
554					m.targetInput, cmd = m.targetInput.Update(msg)
555					m.targetPath = m.targetInput.Value()
556				case 7:
557					m.trivyServerInput, cmd = m.trivyServerInput.Update(msg)
558				case 10:
559					m.gitleaksConfigInput, cmd = m.gitleaksConfigInput.Update(msg)
560				}
561				return m, cmd
562			}
563		}
564	
565		// Handle non-textinput fields
566		switch msg.String() {
567		case "down":
568			m.blurAllTextInputs()
569			m.focusedField = m.nextField()
570			if m.isTextInputField(m.focusedField) {
571				m.focusTextField(m.focusedField)
572			}
573			return m, nil
574		case "up":
575			m.blurAllTextInputs()
576			m.focusedField = m.prevField()
577			if m.isTextInputField(m.focusedField) {
578				m.focusTextField(m.focusedField)
579			}
580			return m, nil
581		case "left":
582			return m.handleFormLeft()
583		case "right":
584			return m.handleFormRight()
585		case "enter":
586			// Enter always starts the scan in this view (Rule 135 — unique action)
587			return m.startScan()
588		case " ":
589			return m.handleFormSpace()
590		case "ctrl+s":
591			return m.startScan()
592		}
593		return m, nil
594	}

597	func (m Model) handleFormLeft() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
598		if m.focusedField == 0 {
599			return m.cycleTargetType("left"), nil
600		}
601		return m, nil
602	}

605	func (m Model) handleFormRight() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

607			return m.cycleTargetType("right"), nil
608		}
609		return m, nil
610	}

612	// cycleTargetType toggles the target type and resets the target input
613	func (m Model) cycleTargetType(_ string) Model {
614		switch m.targetType {
615		case "directory":
616			m.targetType = "image"
617			m.targetInput.Placeholder = "image:tag"
618		case "image":
619			m.targetType = "directory"
620			m.targetInput.Placeholder = "/path/to/scan"
621		}
622		m.targetPath = ""
623		m.targetInput.SetValue("")

628	func (m Model) handleFormSpace() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
629		// Server-incompatible fields cannot be toggled when a Trivy server is set
630		if m.isServerMode() && m.isServerIncompatibleField(m.focusedField) {
631			return m, nil
632		}
633		switch m.focusedField {
634		case 2:
635			m.enableVuln = !m.enableVuln
636			m.saveOptionsToConfig()
637		case 3:
638			m.enableSecret = !m.enableSecret
639			m.saveOptionsToConfig()
640		case 4:
641			m.enableMisconfig = !m.enableMisconfig
642			m.saveOptionsToConfig()

651			m.saveOptionsToConfig()
652		case 9:
653			m.ignoreEOL = !m.ignoreEOL
654			m.saveOptionsToConfig()
655		case 11:
656			m.gitleaksHistory = !m.gitleaksHistory
657			m.saveOptionsToConfig()

38	
39	`internal/ui/status/model.go:64-67` and `internal/ui/status/update.go:57-60`
40	
41	`Model.creating`, `Model.editing` and `Model.confirming` are assigned in five
42	places and read in none: the view keys off `componentForm != nil` and
43	`confirmModal != nil` instead. `HasActiveForm`, the one method that read them, is
44	commented out at `model.go:139`.
45	
46	`ComponentFormCancelledMsg` is never sent either. `ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg`
47	answers `esc` by returning a nil form, and the caller stores that — so the
48	`case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg` branch in `Update()` cannot run. Its
49	body is the only thing that would reset `creating` / `editing`, which is why they
50	would stay true after a cancellation if anything did read them.
51	
52	Harmless today, but it is state that lies: a reader reasonably assumes those
53	flags mean something. Found while writing the phase 2 tests; the tests
54	deliberately assert on `componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags,
55	so removing them breaks nothing.
56	
57	**Fix:** delete the three fields, the unreachable case and the message type — or
58	give `esc` a message and make the flags load-bearing. Deleting is the smaller
59	change and matches how the view already works.
60	
61	### D9 — The containers list opens sorted Z→A
62	
63	`internal/ui/containers/model.go:140-147`
64	
65	`New()` sets neither `sortColumn` nor `sortAsc`, so both take their zero value:
66	name, *descending*. The status view, which has the same cycle-sort mechanism,
67	sets `sortAsc: true` explicitly. The header does show `Name ▼`, so the view is
68	at least honest about it — but nobody chose it, and it disagrees with the other
69	list view in the application.
70	
71	**Fix:** set `sortAsc: true` in `New()`, one line. Left for a deliberate call
72	because it changes what the user sees on open.
73	`TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending` pins the current behaviour and says so.
74	
75	### D10 — A registry failure is invisible until the user focuses the Template field
76	
77	`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:445-449` and `:493-496`
78	
79	When the OCI registry cannot be reached, the explorer opens the creation form
80	anyway and calls `SetTemplateWarning("Registry error: …")` — the right call.
81	But `renderTemplateList` returns early when the field is not focused, so the
82	warning sits below that return and never renders. The user sees a Template
83	field offering nothing but "none", with no indication that the list failed to
84	load rather than being genuinely empty.
85	
86	Reaching it takes four keystrokes: switch the type to Project, then move focus
87	down to Template. Nothing suggests doing so.
88	
89	Found in phase 3 while covering the explorer.
90	`TestTemplateFailureStillOpensTheForm` pins both halves — that the warning is
91	*not* visible on the unfocused field, and that it appears once focused — so the
92	test fails in both directions when this is fixed, and says so.
93	
94	**Fix:** render the warning outside the focused/unfocused branch, or surface it
95	on the form as a whole rather than on the field. Left for a deliberate call
96	because it changes a shared component used by more than the explorer.
97	
98	### D11 — CRITICAL and HIGH look identical in the findings details
99	
100	`internal/ui/security/details.go:155-166`
101	
102	`getSeverityStyle` builds the CRITICAL style by hand as
103	`ColorError` + `Bold(true)`, which is exactly what `theme.StatusErrorStyle`
104	already is — and HIGH returns that. The two are byte-identical, so the severity
105	of a finding is unreadable from its detail view.
106	
107	The theme already defines `ColorSeverityCritical`, `ColorSeverityHigh`,
108	`ColorSeverityMedium` and `ColorSeverityLow`, and the findings *table* uses them
109	through `theme.TableStylesForSeverity`. Only the details view diverges, which
110	also makes it a Rule 102 violation: the style is composed locally instead of
111	coming from the theme.
112	
113	Found in phase 3 while covering the security view.
114	`TestSeverityStylesCollapseCriticalIntoHigh` pins the current behaviour and is
115	deliberately inverted, so it fails when the palette is wired in — which is the
116	fix.
117	
118	**Fix:** return the `ColorSeverity*` styles. Left for a deliberate call because
119	it changes colours the user already reads.
120

122	
123	**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the

125	
126	The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while

129	The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`

`~/.devdesk`, so `TestMain` redirects `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` at a temporary
directory for the whole package and the purge and save commands are **executed**.

so without it the tests would rewrite the developer's own configuration.

Its most worthwhile tests are not about the state machine at all: they are about
`extractMeaningfulLines`, which reduces a wall of Trivy and Gitleaks stderr to
the one line that explains a failure. What it *discards* — INFO lines, progress
bars, the doubled `Fatal error / run error:` wrapping — is the whole feature,
and the fallback that shows the raw text rather than an empty panel is what
stops a novel log format leaving the user with nothing.

39	`internal/ui/status/model.go:64-67` and `internal/ui/status/update.go:57-60`
40	
41	`Model.creating`, `Model.editing` and `Model.confirming` are assigned in five
42	places and read in none: the view keys off `componentForm != nil` and
43	`confirmModal != nil` instead. `HasActiveForm`, the one method that read them, is
44	commented out at `model.go:139`.
45	
46	`ComponentFormCancelledMsg` is never sent either. `ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg`
47	answers `esc` by returning a nil form, and the caller stores that — so the
48	`case components.ComponentFormCancelledMsg` branch in `Update()` cannot run. Its
49	body is the only thing that would reset `creating` / `editing`, which is why they
50	would stay true after a cancellation if anything did read them.
51	
52	Harmless today, but it is state that lies: a reader reasonably assumes those
53	flags mean something. Found while writing the phase 2 tests; the tests
54	deliberately assert on `componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags,
55	so removing them breaks nothing.
56	
57	**Fix:** delete the three fields, the unreachable case and the message type — or
58	give `esc` a message and make the flags load-bearing. Deleting is the smaller
59	change and matches how the view already works.
60	
61	### D9 — The containers list opens sorted Z→A
62	
63	`internal/ui/containers/model.go:140-147`
64	
65	`New()` sets neither `sortColumn` nor `sortAsc`, so both take their zero value:
66	name, *descending*. The status view, which has the same cycle-sort mechanism,
67	sets `sortAsc: true` explicitly. The header does show `Name ▼`, so the view is
68	at least honest about it — but nobody chose it, and it disagrees with the other
69	list view in the application.
70	
71	**Fix:** set `sortAsc: true` in `New()`, one line. Left for a deliberate call
72	because it changes what the user sees on open.
73	`TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending` pins the current behaviour and says so.
74	
75	### D10 — A registry failure is invisible until the user focuses the Template field
76	
77	`internal/ui/components/creation_form.go:445-449` and `:493-496`
78	
79	When the OCI registry cannot be reached, the explorer opens the creation form
80	anyway and calls `SetTemplateWarning("Registry error: …")` — the right call.
81	But `renderTemplateList` returns early when the field is not focused, so the
82	warning sits below that return and never renders. The user sees a Template
83	field offering nothing but "none", with no indication that the list failed to
84	load rather than being genuinely empty.
85	
86	Reaching it takes four keystrokes: switch the type to Project, then move focus
87	down to Template. Nothing suggests doing so.
88	
89	Found in phase 3 while covering the explorer.
90	`TestTemplateFailureStillOpensTheForm` pins both halves — that the warning is
91	*not* visible on the unfocused field, and that it appears once focused — so the
92	test fails in both directions when this is fixed, and says so.
93	
94	**Fix:** render the warning outside the focused/unfocused branch, or surface it
95	on the form as a whole rather than on the field. Left for a deliberate call
96	because it changes a shared component used by more than the explorer.
97	
98	### D11 — CRITICAL and HIGH look identical in the findings details
99	
100	`internal/ui/security/details.go:155-166`
101	
102	`getSeverityStyle` builds the CRITICAL style by hand as
103	`ColorError` + `Bold(true)`, which is exactly what `theme.StatusErrorStyle`
104	already is — and HIGH returns that. The two are byte-identical, so the severity
105	of a finding is unreadable from its detail view.
106	
107	The theme already defines `ColorSeverityCritical`, `ColorSeverityHigh`,
108	`ColorSeverityMedium` and `ColorSeverityLow`, and the findings *table* uses them
109	through `theme.TableStylesForSeverity`. Only the details view diverges, which
110	also makes it a Rule 102 violation: the style is composed locally instead of
111	coming from the theme.
112	
113	Found in phase 3 while covering the security view.
114	`TestSeverityStylesCollapseCriticalIntoHigh` pins the current behaviour and is
115	deliberately inverted, so it fails when the palette is wired in — which is the
116	fix.
117	
118	**Fix:** return the `ColorSeverity*` styles. Left for a deliberate call because
119	it changes colours the user already reads.
120	
121	### 1.1 Fixed
122	
123	**Two views' help advertised keys that do nothing.** Found while writing the
124	phase 2 tests, not previously recorded.
125	
126	The status view's `GetHelpContent` documented `n` for "Add a new monitor" while
127	the binding has been `ctrl+n` since Rule 111 standardised it, and the `/` filter
128	was missing altogether; the empty-state message told the user to "Press [n]" too.
129	The containers view advertised `S` (shell in a new window) in `GetShortcuts()`
130	without documenting it at all.
131	
132	The workspaces view had it too, found in phase 3: `n` and `Enter` documented
133	where the bindings are `ctrl+n` and `enter`, `/` undocumented, and the same
134	stale "Press [n]" in its empty state.
135	
136	`explorer` made it four in a row, though only just: every key was documented
137	except `/`. The check caught it on its first run.
138	
139	`security` broke the streak — its help documents every key its header
140	advertises, across all four states. So the drift was not universal after all;
141	three of the five views that carried it were the ones where a binding had been
142	renamed by Rule 111 and the help was not updated with it.
143	
144	All four are fixed, and every view in `internal/ui` now asserts that each key
145	`GetShortcuts()` advertises appears in `GetHelpContent()` — the check that would
146	have caught the drift when it was introduced.
147	
148	**The explorer acted on a different row than the one highlighted.** Found in
149	phase 3, and the most serious defect the coverage work has turned up.
150	
151	`handleKeyMsg` resolved the cursor against `sortedItems(currentItems())` — the

**Phase 3 is complete.** The three-step order held on all four packages, with the coverage figure unchanged to the statement across every split — including the largest file in the project. Three files remain over the 800-line ceiling, all outside the views phase 3 covered.

## Two defects fixed

**Rule 128 was not honoured anywhere in this view.** `statusMessage` was set in three places — "Added x to .gitleaksignore", "Failed to ignore secret", "No references available" — and the package had no clear timer at all, so whichever happened last stayed on screen until a tab switch happened to reset it. Added `clearStatusCmd`/`clearStatusMsg` and wired all three.

**`parseVersion` reported the wrong version.** It scanned for the first whitespace-separated token starting with `v`, so `gitleaks version 8.18.2` reported its version as **"version"**. A leading `v` now only counts when a digit follows. Its `result[:15]` truncation also became `theme.TruncateWidth` — the sixth and last site of the byte-slicing family the backlog said to look for. Grepping for `[:` on strings across `internal/ui` now returns nothing but slice indexing.

`getSeverityStyle` builds the CRITICAL style by hand as `ColorError` + `Bold(true)`, which is byte-identical to the `theme.StatusErrorStyle` it returns for HIGH. Also a Rule 102 violation — the style is composed locally rather than coming from the theme. Recorded rather than fixed since it changes colours the user already reads; `TestSeverityStylesCollapseCriticalIntoHigh` is deliberately inverted so it fails when someone wires the palette in.

## Testing notes

`HOME` and `USERPROFILE` are redirected for the whole package. That is not optional here: every checkbox toggle calls `config.Save`, so without it the tests would rewrite the developer's own `~/.devdesk`. With the redirect in place the cache commands are **executed** rather than asserted on identity, in line with what explorer settled.

The most worthwhile tests are not about the state machine. `extractMeaningfulLines` reduces a wall of Trivy and Gitleaks stderr to the one line that explains a failure, so the tests are about what it *discards* — INFO lines, progress bars, the doubled `Fatal error / run error:` wrapping — and about the fallback that shows the raw text rather than an empty panel when nothing matches.

## An assumption corrected

The backlog predicted `security` would carry the same help drift as the four views before it. It does not: its help documents every key its header advertises, across all four states. The three views that carried the drift were the ones where Rule 111 renamed a binding and the help was not updated with it.

- [x] Split verified as a pure move: the only non-import difference is a dropped `// Messages` section header.
- [ ] `mise run test-race` — CI (no local C compiler).

**Phase 3 terminée.** Dernier paquet, `security` : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/18 — CI verte.

| | Couverture | `model.go` |
|---|---|---|
| avant | 0 % | 1991 lignes |
| étape 1 (surface) | **52,9 %** | 1991 |
| étape 2 (découpe) | **52,9 %** | **245** |
| étape 3 (complément) | **83,7 %** | 245 |
| global | 49,3 % → **55,3 %** | |

Le bilan de la phase, quatre paquets : netdiag 86,1 %, workspaces 81,3 %, explorer 91,5 %, security 83,7 %. **La découpe n'a jamais bougé la couverture d'un seul statement**, y compris sur le plus gros fichier du projet. Ce n'est plus un pari, c'est la méthode pour les phases 4 et 5. Il reste trois fichiers au-dessus de 800 lignes, tous en dehors des vues couvertes : `oci_resources/update.go`, `app/app.go`, `oci_resources/registry_browser.go`.

**Deux corrections.** La Rule 128 n'était honorée **nulle part** dans cette vue : `statusMessage` était posé à trois endroits et aucun timer n'existait dans le paquet, donc le dernier message restait affiché jusqu'à ce qu'un changement d'onglet le remette à zéro par hasard. Et `parseVersion` cherchait le premier token commençant par `v` — `gitleaks version 8.18.2` affichait donc « version » comme numéro de version. Son `result[:15]` est devenu `theme.TruncateWidth` : c'est le **sixième et dernier site** de la famille byte-vs-rune que le backlog demandait de traquer. Un grep de `[:` sur des strings dans `internal/ui` ne renvoie plus que de l'indexation de slices.

**Une nouvelle entrée D11** : `getSeverityStyle` construit le style CRITICAL à la main en `ColorError` + `Bold`, ce qui est exactement le `StatusErrorStyle` qu'il renvoie pour HIGH — les deux sont identiques octet pour octet. Dans la vue détail, on ne distingue pas un critique d'un high, alors que la table des findings les distingue correctement via `theme.TableStylesForSeverity`. C'est aussi une violation de la Rule 102. Laissée ouverte : ça change des couleurs que tu lis déjà. Le test est volontairement inversé, il cassera quand quelqu'un branchera la palette.

Deux notes de méthode. `HOME` est redirigé pour tout le paquet — ce n'est pas du confort : chaque case cochée appelle `config.Save`, donc sans ça les tests réécriraient ton `~/.devdesk`. Et les tests qui valent le plus cher ne portent pas sur la machine à états mais sur `extractMeaningfulLines`, qui réduit un mur de stderr Trivy/Gitleaks à la ligne qui explique l'échec : ils portent sur ce qui est **jeté** (lignes INFO, barres de progression, le double emballage `Fatal error / run error:`) et sur le repli qui affiche le texte brut plutôt qu'un panneau vide.

Enfin, une hypothèse du backlog corrigée : je prédisais que `security` aurait la même dérive d'aide que les quatre vues précédentes. Non — son aide documente chaque touche annoncée, dans les quatre états. Les trois vues touchées étaient celles où la Rule 111 avait renommé un binding sans que l'aide suive.

**Cinq défauts attendent ta décision** : D4 (Tab→↑/↓ dans la modale de suppression), D8 (flags CRUD morts), D9 (`sortAsc: true` dans containers), D10 (avertissement registre invisible), D11 (couleurs de sévérité). Chacun fait une à trois lignes ; leur seul coût est de changer ce que l'utilisateur voit déjà.

Ensuite : phase 4, `ui/oci_resources` (~1 995 statements, et deux des trois fichiers restants au-dessus du plafond).

refactor: delete the write-only CRUD flags in the status view (D8)

Model.creating, Model.editing and Model.confirming were assigned in five places
and read in none: the view keys off componentForm != nil and confirmModal != nil
instead. HasActiveForm, the one method that read them, had been commented out.

ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg answers esc by returning a nil form and the caller
stores that — so its case in Update() could not run, and that case was the only
thing that reset creating/editing. State that lies is worse than no state: a
reader reasonably assumes those fields mean something.

Deleting is the smaller of the two fixes and matches how the view already
works. Nothing else changes: the tests already asserted on componentForm and
confirmModal rather than on the flags, which is what made this safe.
